title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any unitary gate can be certified device-independently in a quantum network using a single Bell test.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum networks, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method was needed.
method: The author constructs a Bell-type scenario involving multiple parties and uses the observed correlations to certify the implementation of an arbitrary unitary gate via a robust self-testing protocol.
result: It is shown that any unitary gate can be uniquely certified up to local isometries, with robustness bounds provided.
conclusion: This work provides a universal framework for DI certification of quantum gates, advancing quantum network verification and cryptography.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold; the authors explore whether indefinite causal order in quantum processes can violate this principle and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where the two thermalization strokes are arranged in an indefinite causal order using a quantum switch, and analyze the resulting heat flows and work output.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause anomalous heat flow from cold to hot and increase the engine's efficiency beyond the standard Otto cycle limit.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling counterintuitive heat flows and enhanced performance in thermal machines.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly under continuous monitoring, with a Planckian bound on the growth rate.
motivation: To quantify information gain from continuous monitoring in quantum systems and connect entropy growth to fundamental timescales.
method: Simplifies the Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy for quantum systems and applies it to monitored observables, deriving a bound from the energy variance.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by the Planckian time τ_P = ħ/(k_B T), linking quantum dynamics to thermodynamic limits.
conclusion: The Planckian bound provides a universal speed limit on information extraction from quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information theory.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A finite-time refrigeration cycle using three interacting Bose-Einstein condensates is numerically demonstrated, achieving cooling below the bath temperature.
motivation: To explore quantum thermodynamic cycles in interacting many-body systems and understand the role of interactions in finite-time refrigeration.
method: Numerical simulations of three coupled BECs with time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a thermodynamic cycle analogous to a quantum refrigerator.
result: The system acts as a refrigerator, cooling the target BEC below the reservoir temperature, with performance depending on interaction strength and cycle duration.
conclusion: Interacting BECs can serve as a platform for finite-time quantum refrigeration, with interactions playing a key role in performance.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, limiting their predictive power. The authors aim to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Using geometric and information-theoretic arguments, they derive speed limits based on the Bures angle and the quantum Fisher information, applicable to general Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
result: They obtain lower bounds on the evolution time that depend only on the initial and final states and the system's dissipative properties, not on the specific control protocol.
conclusion: These trajectory-independent speed limits offer a more fundamental understanding of the speed of quantum processes and have implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding dimension and decoding success.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs are particularly important, but their optimal performance was only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the optimal success probability for (n, n-1)-QRACs.
result: The constructed QRACs saturate the conjectured bound, proving its optimality for all n. The success probability is exactly (n+1)/(2n).
conclusion: This work provides a complete analytical solution for (n, n-1)-QRACs, confirming the conjectured bound and offering insights into the structure of optimal quantum encoding-decoding schemes.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles to achieve high-rate remote entanglement generation over hundreds of kilometers.
motivation: Current quantum network architectures suffer from bandwidth mismatch between deterministic ion gates and ensemble-based memories, limiting entanglement generation rates. A hybrid node that bridges this gap could significantly speed up remote entanglement distribution.
method: The authors design a hybrid node where a trapped ion is entangled with a broadband photon from a spontaneous parametric down-conversion source, which is then compatible with ensemble-based quantum memories. They analyze the protocol's performance using realistic parameters.
result: The hybrid architecture enables entanglement generation rates orders of magnitude higher than purely ion-based approaches, with potential for high-rate remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a practical path to scalable quantum networks by combining the strengths of deterministic ion gates and multiplexed ensemble memories.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that initial states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system far from equilibrium relaxes faster than one closer to equilibrium. Understanding this effect in open quantum systems can provide insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors study the relaxation of operators in open quantum systems using a Lindblad master equation approach, analyzing the time evolution of operator expectation values and comparing relaxation rates for different initial conditions.
result: They demonstrate the existence of the Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator states that are farther from the steady state exhibit faster relaxation than those initially closer.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of the Mpemba effect to operator dynamics in open quantum systems, contributing to the understanding of non-equilibrium relaxation processes and potentially impacting quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Photon-mediated Entanglement Between Spin Qubits Beyond The Dispersive Regime
authors: Andrei I. Nikitchenko And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei I. Nikitchenko and Guido Burkard

Dispersively coupled distant qubits in a shared cavity can become entangled through virtual photon exchange with energy-conserving phase evolution of their quantum states. This interaction can potentially be accelerated by operating on resonance, allowing for the exchange of real photons. In this th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045420] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates photon-mediated entanglement between spin qubits beyond the dispersive regime, enabling faster entanglement generation via real photon exchange.
motivation: Dispersive coupling is slow; operating on resonance could accelerate entanglement but introduces decoherence. The authors aim to show that resonant coupling can still produce high-fidelity entanglement.
method: They theoretically analyze two spin qubits coupled to a common cavity mode, deriving effective Hamiltonians and solving dynamics in both dispersive and resonant regimes, including dissipation.
result: They find that resonant operation can generate entanglement faster than dispersive coupling while maintaining comparable fidelity under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: Resonant photon-mediated entanglement is a viable route for faster quantum gates in hybrid spin-cavity systems, relevant for quantum networking.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems under sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three sets of definitions for internal energy, work, and heat in the context of sudden quenches, and test them against the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, indicating that not all definitions are thermodynamically consistent.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on choosing appropriate thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, deriving tighter bounds and connecting to thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
motivation: Speed limits are fundamental in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, but classical and quantum formulations were separate. The authors aim to unify them via a common information-theoretic framework.
method: They define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics, and derive speed limit inequalities that bound the rate of change of observables in terms of Fisher information and dynamical activity.
result: The unified speed limits are tighter than previous bounds, and they recover known classical and quantum speed limits as special cases. The framework also reveals connections to thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information provides a unifying perspective for speed limits across classical and quantum regimes, with implications for understanding fundamental limits on dynamics and thermodynamics.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution
authors: Sheng Zhao And Peng-Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhao and Peng-Bo Li

Tripartite interactions are fundamental for realizing quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics, yet their native implementation—particularly among distinct quantum systems—remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid quantum architecture comprising a magnonic mode [in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033074] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid magnon-Andreev-superconducting qubit system that realizes enhanced tripartite interactions, leading to collapse-revival phenomena and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging but essential for quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics.
method: The system couples a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit via a common transmission line resonator, enabling controllable tripartite coupling.
result: Enhanced tripartite interaction strength is achieved, leading to collapse-revival dynamics in the magnon mode and redistribution of entanglement among the three subsystems.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid platform provides a viable route to realize strong tripartite interactions and explore multipartite quantum effects in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the limitations of Gaussian criteria.
method: Derives entanglement witnesses using higher-order moments (e.g., fourth-order) and applies them to non-Gaussian states such as photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
result: The new criteria can detect entanglement in states where Gaussian criteria fail, and are experimentally feasible with homodyne detection.
conclusion: The work provides practical tools for entanglement certification in continuous-variable quantum systems, advancing quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a high-rate entanglement generation scheme between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable fast and efficient entanglement distribution between remote quantum processors, which is essential for scalable quantum networks.
method: The scheme interfaces trapped-ion quantum processors with ensemble-based quantum memories via a spontaneous parametric down-conversion source, using multiplexing to enhance the entanglement generation rate.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates by matching the SPDC source to both ions and memories, with single- and double-click protocols analyzed.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical path to high-rate entanglement distribution for quantum networks, leveraging existing ion and memory technologies.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard device-dependent QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical due to low key rates. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only for certain network nodes.
method: They introduce a protocol where only one node (the central hub) is untrusted, while end nodes are trusted. Security is proven using the entropy accumulation theorem and Bell inequality violations from the untrusted node.
result: The protocol achieves significantly higher key rates than fully DI-QKD in asymmetric star networks, with security against general attacks.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance, suitable for realistic quantum network deployments.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian quantum battery.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in the quantum and classical limits.
result: They find that the quantum battery can achieve higher charging efficiency than any classical counterpart, establishing a quantum advantage bound.
conclusion: The results provide a clear benchmark for quantum advantage in energy storage devices, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the more fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements has not been operationally characterized.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness, using quantum information-theoretic tools.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantitative advantage in steering and randomness generation over incompatible but non-coherent measurements.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a key resource for quantum information tasks, with operational significance beyond simple incompatibility.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information and showing robustness to noise.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but is hindered by noise in quantum networks. The authors aim to show that practical noisy networks can still provide quantum advantage.
method: They derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under various noise models, and analyze the QFI scaling with network size and noise.
result: Quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with QFI scaling linearly with the number of sensors, and the advantage threshold depends on noise strength and network size.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can enable quantum advantage in distributed sensing, providing a practical pathway for near-term quantum sensor networks.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates single microwave photon detection using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity, within circuit QED.
motivation: Detecting single microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but remains challenging due to low energies and noise.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot tunnel-coupled to a lead interacts dispersively with a microwave cavity, and analyze the detection scheme using input-output theory and master equation.
result: They show that under suitable conditions, a single photon can be detected via a change in the current through the quantum dot, with high fidelity and low dark count rate.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path towards efficient single microwave photon detection, leveraging hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting circuits and quantum dots.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption is not fully understood.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled system under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving scaling laws for charging power and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role, and identify optimal driving conditions for maximum power.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental understanding of quantum battery performance and suggest design principles for exploiting collective effects.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement autonomously.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum field to mimic a squeezed environment, providing continuous stabilization.
result: The technique maintains high-fidelity entanglement over extended periods, even under realistic imperfections such as loss and noise.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization via squeezed environments is a viable and efficient approach for robust remote entanglement in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which generates quantum correlations that entangle the qubits autonomously.
result: Stationary qubit entanglement is achieved and characterized, showing high fidelity and resilience to noise.
conclusion: Nonlocal squeezed reservoirs offer a promising platform for scalable entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify the diverse forms of quantum advantage and guide research priorities.
method: The authors survey and categorize different types of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, sensing, and simulation advantages.
result: They identify a rich spectrum of quantum advantages, each with distinct resource requirements and practical implications.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted, and future progress requires targeted efforts in specific domains.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and integrated single tin-vacancy centers; measured cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling via resonance fluorescence and photon correlation techniques.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and high-fidelity entanglement generation capability.
conclusion: This platform is a viable building block for future scalable quantum networks, enabling deterministic entanglement between remote nodes.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, defining a boundary between classical and nonclassical processes using a set of axioms.
result: They show that many processes considered classical actually exhibit intrinsic quantumness, and their rule recovers standard signatures like Bell nonlocality while extending to more general scenarios.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational reassessment of quantumness, with implications for quantum information processing and the identification of resources for quantum advantage.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a tool for generating and maintaining multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir, which drives the system into a desired entangled steady state. The reconfigurability is achieved by tuning the cavity parameters.
result: They show that the scheme can produce various entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against noise. The entanglement is dissipatively stabilized, eliminating the need for active feedback.
conclusion: This work provides a practical platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Photon loss is a major obstacle for quantum information processing; active error correction introduces overhead and measurement noise.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical breakeven point, demonstrating passive error correction that outperforms the uncorrected system.
conclusion: Passive error correction can reach breakeven, offering a low-overhead path to fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms. Understanding and reducing these losses is crucial for advancing hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors optimize the piezoelectric transducer's properties in bulk acoustic resonators, systematically characterizing loss channels such as clamping, material absorption, and two-level systems. They use finite-element simulations and experimental measurements to identify dominant loss sources.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, demonstrating a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics. The optimized resonators show reduced loss and enhanced performance.
conclusion: The work provides a clear path to high-coherence mechanical resonators for quantum applications, highlighting the importance of materials engineering in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods are resource-intensive or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with minimal overhead.
result: Achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with low spacetime volume and only 2D local device connectivity, improving practicality for distributed quantum computing.
conclusion: The protocol offers a resource-efficient way to generate logical Bell pairs, advancing distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, compact and mechanically stable nodes with high photon extraction efficiency are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fibers on a chip, coupled to neutral atoms for efficient photon collection.
result: The device achieves high photon extraction efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by improving photon collection and system stability.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. This work provides a robust, experimentally feasible certification.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify that a measurement cannot be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy successfully certifies non-projective measurements in theory and experiment, providing a practical tool for quantum device certification.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and device-independent protocols.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector as an autonomous machine and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using entropy production and measurement accuracy metrics.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic work.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits on the efficiency of quantum detectors and deepen our understanding of the thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces the impact, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with charge noise being the main limitation that can be mitigated by device design.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity entanglement and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, using random monitoring protocols.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the number of required emitters and improve the loss tolerance of quantum repeater protocols, making them more feasible with near-term technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code generation and asymmetric design offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize the spin defect using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, evaluating electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and single-shot readout selectivity.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume devices are fully characterized, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security framework that integrates device characterization parameters into the security analysis.
result: Provides a method to derive secure key rates that account for device imperfections, enabling practical certification.
conclusion: The framework bridges theory and practice, facilitating standards for QKD device certification.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme effectively enhances the effective coherence time of the qubit by detecting and flagging relaxation errors.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation in quantum computing by converting dominant errors into erasures.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (asymptotic and finite-size), and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with field-tested systems, composable security proofs, and record key rates, while challenges remain in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum networks.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing research addressing security, distance, and integration.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop-scale experiments that would detect entanglement between two quantum probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity using current or near-future technology.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments offering a promising avenue.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching harmonic trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium stationary state.
motivation: To understand how collective switching drives correlations in a simple many-particle system out of equilibrium.
method: Trajectories of Brownian particles in a harmonic trap with randomly switching stiffness are recorded and analyzed.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed, characterized by a correlation length that diverges as the switching rate decreases.
conclusion: The system provides a clean experimental platform for studying nonequilibrium correlations and collective behavior in driven systems.

title: Inverse Clausius Thermodynamics In Run-and-Tumble Dynamics
authors: Oded Farago
abstract:
Author(s): Oded Farago

We establish a mapping between one-dimensional run-and-tumble particle dynamics in the presence of thermal noise, and overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially inhomogeneous temperature field. The approach is formulated as an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework, where the effective temperature …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a mapping between run-and-tumble dynamics and Brownian motion in inhomogeneous temperature, formulating an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamics of active matter systems, specifically run-and-tumble particles, which are out of equilibrium and exhibit complex behavior.
method: Derives an effective temperature description by mapping the run-and-tumble dynamics to overdamped Brownian motion with spatially varying temperature, using an inverse-Clausius approach.
result: The mapping yields an effective temperature that depends on the activity parameters, allowing thermodynamic concepts like Clausius inequality to be applied to active systems.
conclusion: The inverse-Clausius framework provides a thermodynamic interpretation for active matter, bridging non-equilibrium dynamics and equilibrium-like thermodynamics.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational irreversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical limitations from finite resolution and noise impose a fundamental bound on reversibility, which is explored here.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor to model detector noise and operational limits.
result: They show that precision constraints lead to irreversibility even when the mathematical evolution is invertible, providing a thermodynamic-like bound on information recovery.
conclusion: Precision-induced irreversibility is a fundamental feature of non-Hermitian systems, with implications for information processing and thermodynamics in open quantum systems.

title: Detection Of Mpemba Effect Through Observables In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect refers to the anomalous relaxation of a quantum state that, despite being initially farther from the steady state, relaxes faster than a closer counterpart. Detecting such a quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state during its time evoluti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014311] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to detect the quantum Mpemba effect using only observable measurements, without full state tomography.
motivation: Detecting the quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state, which is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to provide a simpler detection method based on observables.
method: The authors derive conditions under which the Mpemba effect can be inferred from the time evolution of a single observable, using open quantum system dynamics and the concept of relaxation rates.
result: They show that for certain observables and initial states, the crossing of relaxation curves indicates the Mpemba effect, and they demonstrate this with examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for detecting anomalous relaxation in open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Thermodynamic Modes Of A Quasiperiodic Mobility-edge System In A Quantum Otto Cycle
authors: Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We investigate thermodynamic operation of a quasiperiodic lattice with an exact mobility edge, described by the Biddle–Das Sarma model. We use this model as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle and map its operating mode as a function of the hopping-range parameter [MATH], the initial and final p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034206] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a quasiperiodic lattice with a mobility edge as the working medium of a quantum Otto cycle, mapping its thermodynamic operating modes.
motivation: To understand how the mobility edge and hopping-range parameter affect the performance of a quantum heat engine, bridging condensed matter physics and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the Biddle–Das Sarma model to describe the quasiperiodic lattice and analyze the quantum Otto cycle by varying the hopping-range parameter and initial/final parameters.
result: They identify different operating modes (e.g., engine, refrigerator) and characterize the efficiency and power output as functions of system parameters.
conclusion: The mobility edge provides a tunable feature that can optimize the thermodynamic cycle, offering insights into designing quantum thermal machines with structured materials.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method allows for consistent thermodynamic analysis of processes that previously exhibited nonmonotonic entropy production.
conclusion: Restoring detailed balance via Dyson maps broadens the applicability of thermodynamic concepts to a wider class of stochastic processes.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic resources under random unitary circuit dynamics, providing analytical and numerical results for the generation of nonstabilizerness.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic (nonstabilizerness) spread in many-body systems is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, as magic is necessary for universal quantum computation.
method: The authors consider random unitary circuits with varying gate sets and use measures of nonstabilizerness (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) to track the dynamics. They employ analytical calculations and numerical simulations for systems up to moderate sizes.
result: They find that magic spreads ballistically with a velocity related to the entanglement velocity, and that the growth of magic saturates to a volume-law scaling. The results are consistent with a hydrodynamic picture.
conclusion: The work establishes a connection between quantum resource theory and many-body dynamics, showing that magic spreads similarly to entanglement but with distinct features, and provides a framework for studying resource generation in random circuits.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Experimental characterization of coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient algorithm implementation and error correction; this work explores a superconducting processor with tunable couplers enabling arbitrary two-qubit gates between any pair of qubits.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with a tunable-coupler architecture, perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize coherent errors, and analyze the impact of residual coupling and crosstalk.
result: They identify dominant coherent error sources, including residual ZZ interactions and control crosstalk, and demonstrate that beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity does not significantly degrade gate fidelities compared to nearest-neighbor designs.
conclusion: The work validates that tunable-coupler architectures can achieve high-fidelity gates in a flexible connectivity graph, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors with improved algorithmic efficiency.

title: Stroboscopic Saturation Of Multiparameter Quantum Limits In Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: Berihu Teklu And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Berihu Teklu and Victor Montenegro

A naturally multiparameter sensing scenario arises in spatially distributed networks of quantum sensors, where each node probes a distinct parameter of interest. In such settings, the central challenges are to achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity under well-defined resource constraints and to explic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033053] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies multiparameter quantum sensing in distributed networks, deriving fundamental limits and showing that stroboscopic control can saturate these limits.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing networks face challenges in achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity under resource constraints, especially for multiple parameters. Understanding the fundamental limits and how to reach them is crucial for practical quantum metrology.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for multiparameter estimation in a distributed sensor network, using quantum Fisher information matrix and Bayesian bounds. They analyze a stroboscopic protocol that periodically applies control operations to the sensors.
result: They derive the multiparameter quantum limits and demonstrate that stroboscopic saturation is possible, achieving the optimal scaling with resources. The protocol outperforms static approaches and is robust to noise.
conclusion: Stroboscopic control provides a practical route to saturate multiparameter quantum limits in distributed sensing, advancing the field of quantum metrology and network-based quantum information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, and its quantum counterpart is of interest for understanding collective behavior in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped ions are individually laser-cooled to realize quantum van der Pol oscillators with controlled nonlinear damping and detuning; synchronization is detected via joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear signatures of frequency locking and phase synchronization are observed, matching theoretical predictions for the quantum van der Pol model.
conclusion: The experiment establishes a platform for studying quantum synchronization and its interplay with dissipation, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum networks.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: Long-lived nuclear memory qudits can store entanglement for quantum networks, but efficient entanglement transfer from electronic qubits to nuclear spins is challenging.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer via controlled interactions in defect centers (e.g., NV centers) to accumulate entanglement between nuclear qudits, leveraging high-spin nuclei for higher-dimensional encoding.
result: Demonstrates that high-fidelity entanglement transfer is achievable with realistic parameters, enabling the distribution of high-dimensional entanglement over quantum networks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward quantum repeaters and quantum networks using defect centers with high-spin nuclei, advancing multi-party quantum communication.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.
