[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitary operations needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful measure of non-Gaussianity, with operational interpretations in terms of resource requirements for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a powerful new tool for understanding and quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing the trade-off between fidelity and complexity.
result: The proposed method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving for several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise. The authors aim to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The paper maps the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel spatially correlated errors.
result: The proposed sequences achieve decoupling from k-local noise with a length that does not depend on the total number of qubits, only on the locality k and code parameters.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for trainability.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, analyzing how noise affects the variance of gradients and the expressivity of the circuit.
result: They show that noise can help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and provide estimates for the loss function concentration under realistic noise models.
conclusion: The work offers a principled link between noise and expressivity, guiding the design of noise-resilient variational algorithms and optimizing training strategies.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum coin flipping) and analyze their security and limitations, also discussing photonic implementations.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, and experimental progress.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is advancing rapidly.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review classifying universal behavior in driven open quantum systems using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in nonequilibrium stationary states, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a method to characterize high-Schmidt-number entanglement witnesses in arbitrary-dimensional systems.
motivation: Understanding the degree of entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number, is crucial for quantum technologies. Existing methods for constructing witnesses are limited to low Schmidt numbers.
method: The authors propose a systematic approach using linear programming and convex optimization to construct optimal entanglement witnesses that can detect states with high Schmidt numbers.
result: They provide explicit examples of witnesses for Schmidt numbers up to 4 in arbitrary dimensions and demonstrate their effectiveness on noisy entangled states.
conclusion: The work advances entanglement detection by enabling the characterization of high-dimensional entanglement, which is important for quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for approximating partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Computing thermodynamic properties of quantum systems is computationally hard in general; efficient algorithms are needed for physically relevant regimes.
method: Uses cluster expansion techniques and quantum belief propagation to derive polynomial-time approximation schemes for the partition function and thermal state sampling.
result: Establishes a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling algorithm for the thermal distribution.
conclusion: Weakly interacting quantum spin systems admit efficient classical algorithms for thermodynamic quantities, bridging quantum many-body physics and computational complexity.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and protocols near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for surpassing classical limits, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the timescale for macroscopic equilibration in translation-invariant free-fermion systems, showing that equilibration occurs within a time proportional to the system size.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum systems equilibrate is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the emergence of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and prove equilibration of coarse-grained density using rigorous mathematical techniques, likely involving Lieb-Robinson bounds or similar tools.
result: They prove that the system equilibrates within a timescale that scales linearly with the system size, providing a rigorous bound on the equilibration time.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous foundation for equilibration timescales in free-fermion systems, contributing to the theoretical understanding of quantum thermalization.

title: Cooperative Emission From Two Coupled Solid-state Quantum Emitters
authors: Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, And Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi
abstract:
Author(s): Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, and Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi

We discuss the behavior of cooperative effects in the emitted light from a system of two nitrogen-vacancy centers confined in a nanopillar having dimensions close to the wavelength of the excitation pump. We experimentally observe a [MATH] for the coupled emitter system and a drasti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013716] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of cooperative emission from two coupled NV centers in a nanopillar, showing superradiance and subradiance.
motivation: Understanding cooperative effects in solid-state quantum emitters is important for quantum information processing and nanophotonics.
method: Two NV centers are confined in a nanopillar near the excitation wavelength; their emission is measured and analyzed for cooperative signatures.
result: Observed enhanced and suppressed emission rates indicative of superradiance and subradiance, with a measured coupling strength.
conclusion: The system demonstrates controllable cooperative emission, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Lindblad Master Equation And Its Nonlinear Extensions Via Quantum Trajectory Averaging
authors: Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, and Shu Chen

Since precisely controlling dissipation in realistic environments is challenging, digital simulation of the Lindblad master equation (LME) is of great significance for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems. However, achieving long-time simulations for complex systems with mul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012436] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a digital quantum simulation method for the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions using quantum trajectory averaging.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is crucial for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics, but long-time simulations of complex systems are challenging. The authors aim to provide a scalable digital simulation approach.
method: The method uses quantum trajectory averaging on a digital quantum computer, encoding the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions (e.g., mean-field and second-order extensions) into quantum circuits.
result: The approach enables efficient simulation of open quantum systems with multiple dissipative channels and nonlinear effects, demonstrating accuracy and scalability for benchmark models.
conclusion: Digital quantum simulation via trajectory averaging is a viable tool for studying open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Quantum Gate Broadcasting On Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Hiroki Sukeno And Tzu-Chieh Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Sukeno and Tzu-Chieh Wei

Using a generalized quantum gate teleportation protocol, copies of a gate encoding a known or unknown parameter can be sent to multiple receivers. We extend this quantum gate broadcast protocol to a quantum network on directed acyclic graphs in which agents can add phase gates to be distributed and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012611] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Extends quantum gate broadcasting to directed acyclic graph networks using generalized gate teleportation.
motivation: Quantum gate broadcasting allows a single gate to be applied to multiple receivers, which is useful for distributed quantum computing and quantum networks.
method: Generalizes the quantum gate teleportation protocol to directed acyclic graphs, enabling agents to add phase gates for distribution.
result: Demonstrates that gate broadcasting can be performed on arbitrary directed acyclic graph topologies.
conclusion: Provides a framework for quantum gate distribution in network settings, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize response theory beyond linear response near equilibrium.
method: The authors use a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving mutual linearity relations from the structure of the master equation without assuming detailed balance.
result: They show that two observables are linearly dependent even far from equilibrium, with coefficients determined by the stationary distribution and the perturbation.
conclusion: The mutual linearity provides a new framework for nonequilibrium response theory, applicable to a wide class of stochastic systems.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for arbitrary manipulation of nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on nuclear spins via the boron vacancy center.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radio-frequency pulses to achieve universal control over the nuclear spin qubit.
result: The protocol enables arbitrary rotations of the nuclear spin state with high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway for using hBN as a platform for quantum information processing, leveraging its nuclear spins for scalable quantum computing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and engineered interactions to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating control over the quantum state of a harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating nonclassical states, with potential applications in quantum sensing, quantum information processing, and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a composable security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization.
result: They achieve record secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum communication closer to practical deployment, especially for metropolitan quantum networks.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around the atom array, reducing blackbody radiation. They measure Rydberg lifetimes at cryogenic temperatures and compare with room-temperature baselines.
result: Rydberg lifetimes are significantly extended at cryogenic temperatures, with measured lifetimes exceeding theoretical predictions for blackbody-limited decay, indicating suppression of relaxation errors.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to mitigate dominant relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers, potentially enabling higher-fidelity two-qubit gates.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling design that reduces unwanted transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a practical improvement for superconducting qubit readout, relevant for quantum computing hardware.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown quantum systems, such as spin environments, is crucial for quantum technologies but challenging due to high dimensionality and noise.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that simultaneously performs model selection and parameter estimation, enabling fast and scalable analysis of multidimensional quantum systems.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize compact, scalable quantum security devices that do not require trust in the hardware, leveraging self-testing protocols for randomness generation.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip integrating all necessary components for a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, including entangled photon sources and measurement devices.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a self-testing protocol, showing that device-independent quantum randomness expansion can be achieved on a photonic chip.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, miniaturized quantum security devices by demonstrating a fully integrated self-testing QRNG on a chip.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Electron spin qubits are key for quantum technologies, but their coherence times are limited by environmental noise. Predicting these times accurately is crucial for designing better qubits.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing how to handle higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for cases with strong higher-order contributions or surface-induced decoherence.
conclusion: Computational predictions of spin qubit decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the development of solid-state quantum technologies.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Calibration-Free Non-Markovian Noise Suppression
authors: Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, and Dawei Lu

Non-Markovian noise, arising from environmental memory effects, is the most general and challenging form of noise in quantum computing, and is typically difficult to characterize and suppress. Here, we analyze and experimentally demonstrate a non-Markovian noise suppression scheme inspired by quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030601] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a calibration-free non-Markovian noise suppression scheme using quantum control techniques.
motivation: Non-Markovian noise is a major obstacle in quantum computing, and existing suppression methods often require precise calibration or characterization.
method: The scheme is inspired by quantum error correction and uses dynamical decoupling pulses that are robust to calibration errors, implemented on a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) platform.
result: The method effectively suppresses non-Markovian noise without requiring calibration, as demonstrated experimentally.
conclusion: Calibration-free suppression of non-Markovian noise is feasible, offering a practical approach for improving quantum gate fidelity in realistic noisy environments.

title: Engineering Quantum Noise Interference With Squeezed Vacuum In Dissipative Optomechanics
authors: Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, And Huaizhi Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, and Huaizhi Wu

Quantum noises impose limits on both backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators. Here, we demonstrate that for dissipative optomechanical systems in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable supp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise in dissipative optomechanical systems.
motivation: Quantum noise limits backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators; the authors aim to overcome these limits using squeezed light and Fano interference.
method: They theoretically analyze a dissipative optomechanical system in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, incorporating squeezed vacuum to engineer Fano interference and suppress quantum noise.
result: Broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise is achieved, improving the performance of optomechanical devices.
conclusion: Squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference is an effective technique for quantum noise mitigation in dissipative optomechanics, with potential applications in quantum sensing and transduction.

title: Connecting Magic Dynamics In Thermofield Double States To Spectral Form Factors
authors: Ning Sun And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Sun and Pengfei Zhang

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. The hardness of classical simulation within the stabilizer formalism, commonly referred to as magic resources, can be quantified by the stabi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030401] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Connects magic resource dynamics in thermofield double states to spectral form factors, linking quantum chaos and complexity.
motivation: To understand the growth of quantum complexity in chaotic systems and its relation to spectral properties.
method: Analytical calculations and numerical simulations of stabilizer entropy (magic) in thermofield double states under unitary evolution.
result: The magic dynamics exhibit a ramp-plateau structure analogous to spectral form factors, with the plateau height related to the Hilbert space dimension.
conclusion: Magic dynamics in chaotic systems can be understood via spectral form factors, providing a bridge between quantum information and quantum chaos.

title: Electron Dynamics Induced By Quantum Cat-state Light
authors: Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, And Naoto Tsuji
abstract:
Author(s): Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, and Naoto Tsuji

The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light. They show that the light’s quantum interference is imprinted onto electronic coherence and entanglement through interferential non-Hermitian dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light, showing that quantum interference of light imprints onto electronic coherence and entanglement via non-Hermitian dynamics.
motivation: To understand how quantum properties of light, specifically cat states, can influence electron dynamics in hybrid quantum systems, potentially enabling new ways to control electronic coherence and entanglement.
method: The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory that captures the effect of Schrödinger-cat-state light on electrons, using non-Hermitian dynamics to describe the interferential effects.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum interference of the cat-state light is transferred to the electronic system, creating electronic coherence and entanglement that depend on the cat-state parameters.
conclusion: This work reveals a mechanism for imprinting quantum optical properties onto electronic systems, which could be useful for quantum information processing in hybrid light-matter platforms.

title: Resonant Blockade In Driven Quantum Oscillators
authors: B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

We investigate the emergence of synchronization blockade arising from the combined action of external driving and internal exchange interactions in quantum oscillators. The external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode through coupling to the driven mode, leading to a breakdown of limit cyc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012210] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates synchronization blockade in driven quantum oscillators due to external driving and internal exchange interactions.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics, as it relates to collective dynamics and energy flow.
method: The authors study a system of two coupled quantum oscillators with one driven externally, analyzing the breakdown of limit cycles and the emergence of a resonant blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the external drive indirectly affects the undriven mode through coupling, leading to a resonant blockade that suppresses synchronization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum synchronization phenomena, which may have implications for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Linear-optical Schemes To Postselect High-dimensional Dicke States
authors: Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, And Seungbeom Chin
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, and Seungbeom Chin

Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear-optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013714] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes linear-optical schemes to postselect high-dimensional Dicke states, which are multipartite entangled states useful for quantum information applications.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is essential for distributed quantum applications, and high-dimensional Dicke states offer advantages but are challenging to prepare.
method: The authors design linear-optical interference setups with postselection to herald the generation of high-dimensional Dicke states from independent photons.
result: The schemes achieve high success probabilities and fidelities for certain parameter regimes, demonstrating feasibility with current technology.
conclusion: The proposed linear-optical methods provide a practical route to generate high-dimensional Dicke states, advancing multipartite entanglement resources.

title: Entanglement Cohomology For Ghz And W States
authors: Christian Ferko And Keiichiro Furuya
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ferko and Keiichiro Furuya

Entanglement cohomology assigns a graded cohomology ring to a multipartite pure state, providing homological invariants that are stable under local unitaries and characterize inequivalent patterns of entanglement. In this work we derive exact expressions for the dimensions of these cohomology groups…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012437] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces entanglement cohomology, a new homological invariant for multipartite pure states, and computes it for GHZ and W states.
motivation: To develop a systematic classification of multipartite entanglement patterns beyond existing measures, using cohomology theory.
method: The authors define a graded cohomology ring from the entanglement structure of a pure state and derive exact formulas for the dimensions of cohomology groups for GHZ and W states.
result: Exact expressions for the cohomology dimensions are obtained, showing that GHZ and W states have distinct cohomological signatures.
conclusion: Entanglement cohomology provides a new set of invariants that distinguish inequivalent entanglement patterns, offering a novel tool for entanglement theory.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of Time Translation Symmetry Via Spatially Inhomogeneous Many-body Interactions
authors: Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, and Xiangdong Zhang

Time crystals, with their intrinsic long-range temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, provide a unique platform for quantum applications that leverages long-lived coherence. We investigate the emergence of time-crystalline order in a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice featuring…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012612] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates spontaneous time translation symmetry breaking in a driven dissipative atomic lattice, realizing a time crystal phase.
motivation: Time crystals exhibit long-lived temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, offering a platform for quantum applications that leverage coherence.
method: The authors study a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice with spatially inhomogeneous many-body interactions, analyzing the emergence of time-crystalline order.
result: They show that spatially inhomogeneous interactions can stabilize a time crystal phase with robust oscillations.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for realizing time crystals, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phases of matter.

title: Dicke States For Two Accelerated Two-level Atoms
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Charles A. Wallace, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We study two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms moving in the right Rindler wedge and interacting with a massless scalar field. Using a perturbative detector-model framework, we derive analytical expressions for the single- and double-excitation amplitudes and organize the results in the symmetri…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012813] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two uniformly accelerated two-level atoms interacting with a scalar field, deriving excitation amplitudes and analyzing Dicke states in the context of acceleration.
motivation: To understand how acceleration affects quantum correlations and collective behavior in atomic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics in non-inertial frames.
method: Using a perturbative detector-model framework, analytical expressions for single- and double-excitation amplitudes are derived, and results are organized in symmetrized Dicke states.
result: Analytical expressions for excitation amplitudes are obtained, showing how acceleration modifies the collective atomic dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between acceleration and quantum coherence, with implications for quantum thermodynamics in curved spacetimes.

title: Light-induced Quantum Self-trapping Of Vibrational Excitons In An Optical Cavity
authors: Vincent Pouthier And Saad Yalouz
abstract:
Author(s): Vincent Pouthier and Saad Yalouz

In an optical cavity, strong light-matter coupling between excitons and photons has been widely reported as a way to enhance energy delocalization through spatially extended polaritonic states. In contrast, leveraging cavity-mediated light-matter effects to promote the reciprocal phenomenon, namely,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013116] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that strong light-matter coupling in an optical cavity can induce quantum self-trapping of vibrational excitons, counteracting the usual delocalization effect.
motivation: To explore how cavity-mediated light-matter interactions can localize rather than delocalize excitons, potentially enabling new control over energy transport in molecular systems.
method: The authors model a molecular crystal coupled to an optical cavity using a Holstein-like Hamiltonian and solve for the dynamics of vibrational excitons under strong coupling conditions.
result: They find a transition from delocalized polaritonic states to self-trapped exciton states when the light-matter coupling exceeds a threshold, characterized by a nonlinear dependence on coupling strength.
conclusion: Cavity-induced self-trapping offers a mechanism to control exciton localization, which could be relevant for quantum information processing and energy transfer applications.

title: Physically Motivated Guiding States For Local Hamiltonians
authors: Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, and Michael J. Bremner

We study the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem: given a local Hamiltonian [MATH] together with a classical description of a guiding state that has non-negligible overlap with the ground state of [MATH], estimate the ground-state energy within inverse-polynomial precision. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012431] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem, where a guiding state with non-negligible overlap with the ground state is provided, and shows that it is QCMA-complete.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of estimating ground-state energies with a guiding state is important for quantum algorithms and quantum complexity theory.
method: The authors prove QCMA-completeness of the guided local Hamiltonian problem by constructing a reduction from a QCMA-complete problem and analyzing the overlap condition.
result: The guided local Hamiltonian problem is QCMA-complete, meaning it is as hard as problems solvable by a quantum verifier with a classical witness.
conclusion: Providing a guiding state does not reduce the complexity class from QMA to a simpler class; the problem remains hard even with a good guiding state.

title: Extended Thermodynamics Of Optimal Networks
authors: Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, And Lamberto Rondoni
abstract:
Author(s): Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, and Lamberto Rondoni

We introduce a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks based on generalized transport potentials (GTPs). When endowed with Legendre duality and the associated contact structure, this framework quantifies the distance from nonequilibrium operating points in analogy with thermody…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014135] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks using generalized transport potentials and Legendre duality.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic concepts to optimal transport networks, quantifying nonequilibrium operating points.
method: Introduces generalized transport potentials (GTPs) with Legendre duality and contact structure, analogous to equilibrium thermodynamics.
result: Provides a framework to measure distance from equilibrium and optimize network performance.
conclusion: The formalism offers a unified thermodynamic perspective for analyzing and designing optimal transport networks.

title: Probing Eigenstate Thermalization In The Weakly Interacting Holstein Polaron Model
authors: K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, And C. Sudheesh
abstract:
Author(s): K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, and C. Sudheesh

The origin of chaos in quantum systems remains a central challenge in many-body physics. Here, we use the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) as a tool to investigate the transition from integrability to chaos in the one-dimensional Holstein polaron model. By combining exact diagonalization with an anal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014118] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the adiabatic gauge potential to probe the transition from integrability to chaos in the Holstein polaron model, linking to eigenstate thermalization.
motivation: Understanding the origin of chaos in quantum many-body systems is a central challenge; the Holstein polaron model serves as a testbed for thermalization.
method: Exact diagonalization combined with analysis of the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) to diagnose chaos and integrability breaking.
result: The AGP effectively detects the onset of chaos and thermalization in the weakly interacting regime.
conclusion: The AGP is a useful tool for probing eigenstate thermalization in interacting quantum systems.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model for Sagnac-based electro-optic encoders and explores modulation strategies for high-speed quantum communication.
motivation: Faster modulation schemes are needed for quantum communication; Sagnac-based encoders offer stability and high speed but lack a unified theoretical model.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies, including phase and intensity modulation, using numerical simulations.
result: They identify optimal modulation strategies that achieve high extinction ratios and low error rates, suitable for quantum key distribution and other quantum network applications.
conclusion: The proposed model and strategies enable practical high-speed quantum communication systems, advancing quantum network hardware.

title: Double-bracket Quantum Algorithms For High-fidelity Ground-state Preparation
authors: Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, And Marek Gluza
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, and Marek Gluza

Ground-state preparation is a central application for quantum computers but remains challenging in practice. In this work, we quantitatively investigate the performance and gate counts of double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) for ground-state preparation. We propose a practical strategy in which…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033078] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and benchmarks double-bracket quantum algorithms for high-fidelity ground-state preparation, focusing on practical gate counts and performance.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is crucial for quantum computing applications like quantum chemistry and optimization, but existing methods often require deep circuits. The authors aim to develop a more efficient algorithm.
method: The authors introduce double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) that use a sequence of double-bracket rotations to iteratively reduce the energy of a trial state. They analyze the gate complexity and optimize the protocol for near-term devices.
result: DBQAs achieve high-fidelity ground-state preparation with significantly fewer gates compared to standard approaches like adiabatic state preparation or variational methods, as demonstrated on several model Hamiltonians.
conclusion: Double-bracket quantum algorithms offer a promising practical route for ground-state preparation on near-term quantum computers, balancing fidelity and circuit depth.

title: Inhomogeneous Mass Trap For Dark-state Polaritons In Atomic Media
authors: Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, And Wen-Te Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, and Wen-Te Liao

Spatially structured control fields generate an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium, enabling tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032006] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an inhomogeneous mass trap for dark-state polaritons in an atomic medium using spatially structured control fields, enabling tunable bound states and coherent dynamics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control and trapping of dark-state polaritons, which are crucial for quantum information storage and processing in atomic ensembles.
method: The authors use spatially structured control fields in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) medium to create an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons.
result: They show that the trap can support tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics, with potential for quantum memory and manipulation.
conclusion: The inhomogeneous mass trap provides a new tool for controlling dark-state polaritons, advancing hybrid quantum systems that combine atomic media with light fields.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor provides a rigorous and efficient approach.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulation of complex open quantum systems.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse fields, including quantum thermodynamics, condensed matter, and quantum optics, with efficient numerical implementations.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian dynamics, with potential for further development and broader applications.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, as evidenced by the simulation of complex many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve practical quantum computational advantage, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-robust approach using entangled states.
method: The authors introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise. They analyze the sensitivity and robustness of these states for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states provide a quantum advantage in differential phase sensing while being inherently immune to common-mode noise, enabling practical sensor networks.
conclusion: This work offers a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, leveraging entanglement for metrological gain without requiring complex noise mitigation.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout; this work addresses that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms for quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local nondestructive readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg states.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for systematic optimization of quantum light sources, significantly increasing the success rate of generating essential quantum states.
motivation: Scalable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods lack systematic optimization and have low success rates.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank, enabling systematic optimization of optical non-Gaussian state generation through a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration.
result: The new control parameters allow orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states, such as cat states and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable optical non-Gaussian state generation, advancing quantum computing and communication with continuous-variable systems.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation, driven by phase transitions, can serve as a computational framework for cells to process high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex, high-dimensional signals to respond appropriately, but traditional molecular signaling pathways may be insufficient. Phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase transitions in biomolecular condensates and computational primitives, discussing how condensation can implement classification, sensing, and decision-making.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform computations that are robust, sensitive, and capable of integrating multiple signals, potentially explaining how cells achieve complex behaviors.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental investigation.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is relevant to understanding qubit leakage in superconducting qubits.
motivation: Transmon ionization can cause qubits to escape their computational states, degrading performance; understanding this process is crucial for improving readout and coherence.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance pathways leading to ionization.
result: They observe clear signatures of Landau-Zener transitions and quantify the ionization rates under various drive conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon leakage mechanisms, which can inform better qubit designs and readout schemes to mitigate ionization.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms, including their small mass and long-range interactions, and propose experimental implementations using optical tweezers and laser cooling techniques.
result: Helium-3 atoms offer benefits such as faster tunneling rates and stronger interactions compared to other atomic species, enabling new regimes for quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms present a promising platform for advancing quantum science, particularly in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue for achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system and use them to perform displacement sensing, optimizing the measurement protocol.
result: They achieve optimal displacement sensing performance, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulse sequences to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that uses numerical optimization to design high-fidelity multiqubit gates in Rydberg atom arrays, considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework yields gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% for multiqubit gates, demonstrating feasibility for quantum error correction codes.
conclusion: The optimized multiqubit gates bring neutral-atom platforms closer to practical quantum error correction, advancing the hybrid quantum systems direction.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The framework uses a moment-matching technique to construct a unitary dilation on a 1D tight-binding lattice, reducing the required ancillary qubits and connectivity.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient framework for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and algorithm design.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise spectroscopy in quantum devices, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence sources.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores whether collective effects in an ensemble can enhance photon blockade.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a viable route to achieve strong photon blockade without demanding single-emitter parameters, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction and high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction and hardware-specific optimizations to reduce space and time overhead.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The transversal architecture demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
