[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum singular value transformation.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, comparing resource requirements and applicability of different approaches.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource constraints.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems in various fields, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to relate them. This review aims to unify these approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and then survey various numerical techniques such as hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes and applications.
conclusion: A unified perspective on non-Markovian simulation methods is valuable for advancing quantum technologies and fundamental physics, though the paper is a review rather than presenting novel results.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum circuits, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve the efficiency of quantum algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, though challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Synchronized Aharonov-Bohm Motifs Via Engineered Dissipation
authors: Christopher W. Wächtler And Gloria Platero
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher W. Wächtler and Gloria Platero

The interplay between external gauge fields and lattice geometry can induce extreme localization dynamics through complete destructive interference. We show that combining this flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030405] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that combining flux-induced localization with engineered dissipation leads to robust spin synchronization in rotationally symmetric spin systems.
motivation: Understanding how to achieve robust synchronization in quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and network applications.
method: The authors study a rotationally symmetric spin system under an external gauge field (Aharonov-Bohm effect) and introduce engineered dissipation to stabilize synchronized states.
result: They demonstrate that the interplay of flux-induced localization and dissipation yields robust spin synchronization, protected against certain perturbations.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation can be used to create and stabilize synchronized quantum states, offering a new tool for quantum control and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Imaginarity As A Resource Within Quantum Coherence: Geometric Decomposition And Operational Conversion
authors: Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, and Shao-Ming Fei

We establish a rigorous framework that identifies imaginarity as a fundamental resource inherent in quantum coherence. By means of a geometric decomposition, we partition coherence into distinct imaginarity and residual components, thereby revealing a universal hierarchical relationship among these …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012435] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes imaginarity as a resource within quantum coherence via geometric decomposition and operational conversion.
motivation: To formalize imaginarity as a distinct resource in quantum coherence and understand its role in quantum information tasks.
method: The authors use a geometric decomposition to separate coherence into imaginarity and residual components, and derive conversion relations between these resources.
result: They reveal a universal hierarchical relationship among imaginarity and coherence, and provide operational interpretations for imaginarity conversion.
conclusion: Imaginarity is a fundamental resource that can be quantified and converted, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Wiener Architecture For Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Alessio Benavoli And Felix C. Binder
abstract:
Author(s): Alessio Benavoli and Felix C. Binder

This work focuses on quantum reservoir computing and, in particular, on quantum Wiener architectures (qWiener), consisting of quantum linear dynamic networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear static readouts. We provide the first rigorous proof that qWiener systems retain the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012433] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides the first rigorous proof that quantum Wiener systems, consisting of linear quantum dynamics with weak measurements and classical nonlinear readouts, retain the universal approximation property for fading memory nonlinear functionals.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising paradigm for temporal information processing, but rigorous theoretical foundations for architectures with continuous measurements were lacking.
method: The authors analyze quantum Wiener architectures, which combine linear quantum dynamics, weak continuous measurements, and classical nonlinear readouts, and prove their universality using the theory of Volterra series and fading memory.
result: They prove that qWiener systems can approximate any fading memory nonlinear functional with arbitrary precision, establishing a theoretical basis for quantum reservoir computing with continuous measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a rigorous foundation for quantum reservoir computing with continuous measurements, opening the door to practical implementations and further theoretical developments.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm that allows a client to outsource VQA computation to an untrusted quantum server while ensuring correctness.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices, but small-scale users lack access to powerful quantum hardware. Delegating computation to a quantum cloud raises trust issues, so verifiability is needed.
method: The authors design a protocol where the client uses a classical computer and a limited quantum device to delegate VQA tasks to a server, employing trap qubits and measurement-based verification to detect cheating.
result: The protocol achieves end-to-end verifiability with only logarithmic overhead in the number of qubits, and is proven secure against malicious servers under standard assumptions.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated VQAs are feasible and efficient, enabling secure quantum cloud computing for near-term applications.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum circuits classically is hard, but for small subregions of the landscape, efficient classical surrogates may be possible, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from classical shadow tomography or compressed sensing.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points in the landscape, reducing the need for many quantum evaluations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantum circuit optimization and variational algorithms, bridging quantum and classical computation.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation
authors: Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, And Xiaoguang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeping Liu, Yaotian Li, Zhaoyu Fei, and Xiaoguang Wang

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary time crystals in open quantum systems beyond mean-field theory using a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation.
motivation: Boundary time crystals are exotic dissipative quantum phases that break time-translation symmetry, but their finite-size behavior and beyond-mean-field corrections are not well understood.
method: The authors develop a stroboscopic rotating-wave approximation to treat the dissipative dynamics analytically and compare with exact numerical simulations.
result: They find that the approximation captures the decay of oscillations and the phase transition, and reveals corrections to the mean-field predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a more accurate description of boundary time crystals in finite systems, highlighting the role of quantum fluctuations.

title: Random-matrix Perspective On Probabilistic Error Cancellation
authors: Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, And David J. Luitz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonhard Moske, Pedro Ribeiro, Tomaž Prosen, Sergiy Denysov, Karol Życzkowski, and David J. Luitz

Probabilistic error cancellation is an attempt to reverse the effect of dissipative noise channels on quantum computers by applying unphysical channels after the execution of a quantum algorithm on noisy hardware. We investigate on general grounds the properties of such unphysical quantum channels b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012442] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes probabilistic error cancellation using random matrix theory to understand the properties of unphysical channels required for error mitigation.
motivation: Probabilistic error cancellation is a promising error mitigation technique for near-term quantum computers, but the properties of the required unphysical channels are not well understood.
method: The authors use random matrix theory to model the noise channels and derive statistical properties of the quasi-probability distributions needed for error cancellation.
result: They find that the required quasi-probabilities can be large and highly non-classical, leading to a significant sampling overhead that scales exponentially with the number of qubits.
conclusion: Probabilistic error cancellation may be impractical for large-scale quantum computers due to the exponential overhead, highlighting the need for more efficient error mitigation techniques.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. Here, different initial many-body configurations evolve toward one of several fixed points, which are macroscopically distinguishable through an order parameter. This mechanism enables state classification in quantum cellular automata a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012209] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum cellular automata near a phase transition to classify initial states, demonstrating a classification capability.
motivation: To explore how ergodicity breaking near phase transitions can be harnessed for state classification in quantum systems.
method: The authors train a quantum cellular automaton to classify different initial many-body configurations based on the order parameter of the fixed points they evolve to.
result: The quantum cellular automaton successfully classifies initial states, showing that phase transitions can serve as a classification mechanism.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions can perform classification tasks, linking many-body physics to machine learning concepts.

title: Fermion Doubling In Dirac Quantum Walks
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We consider discrete spacetime models known as quantum walks, which can be used to simulate Dirac particles. In particular, we look at fermion doubling in these models, in which high-momentum states yield additional low-energy solutions which behave like Dirac particles. The presence of doublers car…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012208] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fermion doubling in Dirac quantum walks, a discrete spacetime model for simulating Dirac particles.
motivation: Fermion doubling is a known issue in lattice field theory, and understanding it in quantum walks is important for quantum simulation of relativistic particles.
method: The authors analyze the dispersion relation of Dirac quantum walks on a lattice and identify conditions under which doublers appear, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They show that fermion doubling is generic in these models and characterize the number and properties of doublers.
conclusion: The work highlights a fundamental limitation of using quantum walks for simulating Dirac fermions, which may inform the design of improved simulation schemes.

title: Long-term Stability Of Quantum Resources Through Gravitational Cat States In A Dissipative Markovian Environment
authors: Anas Ait Chlih And Tamer A. Seoudy
abstract:
Author(s): Anas Ait Chlih and Tamer A. Seoudy

The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the long-term stability of quantum resources (entanglement, discord, coherence) in a gravitational cat state under a dissipative Markovian environment.
motivation: Understanding how gravity affects quantum resources is important for quantum-gravitational interfaces, but the paper focuses on resource preservation rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic fundamentals.
method: The authors model a gravitational cat state interacting with a dissipative Markovian environment and analyze the dynamics of entanglement, discord, and coherence using standard measures.
result: They find that certain quantum resources can be stabilized over long times under specific conditions, but the results are incremental and do not introduce new theoretical tools.
conclusion: The work provides insights into resource stability but is not a core contribution to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Non-Markovian Renormalization Of Optomechanical Exceptional Points
authors: Aritra Ghosh And M. Bhattacharya
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Ghosh and M. Bhattacharya

We investigate how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation affects exceptional points in linearized optomechanical systems with red-sideband drive. For a chosen non-Ohmic mechanical bath, we derive analytical conditions for the memory-renormalized exceptional point by employing a pseudomode mapping, th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013516] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian mechanical dissipation renormalizes exceptional points in optomechanical systems.
motivation: Exceptional points in optomechanics are sensitive to dissipation, and non-Markovian effects can alter their properties, which is important for understanding open quantum systems.
method: The authors use a pseudomode mapping to derive analytical conditions for memory-renormalized exceptional points in a linearized optomechanical system with a non-Ohmic bath.
result: They find that non-Markovian dissipation shifts the exceptional point and modifies the system's dynamics compared to the Markovian case.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects must be accounted for in optomechanical systems to accurately predict exceptional point behavior, impacting applications like sensing.

title: Quantum Complexity In Rule-based Constrained Many-body Models: Scars, Fragmentation, And Chaos
authors: Arkaprava Sil And Sudipto Singha Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprava Sil and Sudipto Singha Roy

Kinetic constraints in quantum many-body systems strongly restrict the accessible Hilbert space, giving rise to highly nontrivial dynamical behavior. In recent years, such systems have attracted growing interest as they provide insight into mechanisms of thermalization and into regimes where thermal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024312] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars, Hilbert space fragmentation, and chaos in constrained models, linking them to thermalization and complexity.
motivation: Understanding how kinetic constraints lead to non-thermal behavior and how complexity measures can characterize these phenomena.
method: Analyzes a family of constrained many-body models with exact solutions, computing level statistics, entanglement entropy, and Krylov complexity.
result: Identifies regimes of quantum scars and fragmentation, and shows that Krylov complexity captures the onset of chaos and distinguishes integrable from chaotic dynamics.
conclusion: Constrained models provide a rich playground for exploring the interplay between quantum complexity, thermalization, and ergodicity breaking.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, focusing on caloric phenomena and engine efficiency.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems as working media in heat engines.
method: Using linear spin-wave theory, the authors analyze the caloric responses and Stirling-cycle efficiency of the Heisenberg-Kitaev model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
result: The DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of DM interactions in quantum thermodynamic cycles, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core information thermodynamics interests.

title: Generic Signatures Of non-Markovian Dynamics In The Presence Of A Magnetic Field
authors: Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, And Bidhan Chandra Bag
abstract:
Author(s): Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, and Bidhan Chandra Bag

In this paper, we have presented the three-dimensional dynamics in the velocity space of a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath in the presence of a magnetic field (MF), as well as external deterministic and stochastic force fields. The directions of the MF and the deterministic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014121] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, focusing on velocity-space signatures.
motivation: To understand how non-Markovian effects manifest in the presence of a magnetic field, which is relevant for open quantum systems and stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive a three-dimensional Langevin equation for a Brownian particle in a magnetic field with non-Markovian thermal bath, and analyze velocity correlation functions and mean squared displacement.
result: They find that non-Markovianity leads to oscillatory behavior in velocity correlations and modifies the diffusion coefficient, with signatures depending on magnetic field strength.
conclusion: The work provides generic signatures of non-Markovian dynamics in magnetic fields, which could be tested experimentally and inform models of quantum Brownian motion.

title: Access-limited Equilibration And Observable-dependent Relaxation In Lattice-gas Systems
authors: Marvin A. Albao
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin A. Albao

We investigate equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted coupling to a particle reservoir. Using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, we isolate the role of reservoir-access geometry by comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014124] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibration dynamics in a lattice-gas model with spatially restricted reservoir access using kinetic Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand how the geometry of reservoir coupling affects equilibration and relaxation in many-body systems.
method: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations comparing spatially uniform exchange with exchange confined to a limited access region.
result: The access-limited geometry leads to observable-dependent relaxation and non-exponential equilibration dynamics.
conclusion: Spatial restrictions on reservoir coupling can significantly alter equilibration behavior, relevant for understanding non-equilibrium thermodynamics in confined systems.

title: Recursive Analytical Technique For The Quantum Analysis Of A Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Parameter Reduction
authors: Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, And Yanne K. Chembo
abstract:
Author(s): Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, and Yanne K. Chembo

An analytic technique for the investigation of the combined impacts of multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density on the measurement of a Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) parameter is introduced. We demonstrate this technique for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033075] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analytic technique to study the combined effects of multiple photon pairs and non-negligible joint spectral density on CHSH parameter measurement.
motivation: Accurate measurement of the CHSH parameter is crucial for Bell inequality tests, but realistic experimental imperfections like multiple photon pairs and spectral correlations degrade the observed violation.
method: The authors develop a recursive analytic technique that incorporates the joint spectral density of photon pairs and accounts for multi-pair contributions in a Gaussian-normal spectral model.
result: The technique quantifies how the CHSH parameter is reduced due to these imperfections, providing a theoretical framework to predict experimental outcomes.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for designing and interpreting Bell tests, but the contribution is incremental and focused on a specific experimental scenario rather than advancing fundamental theory.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, addressing the ambiguity in biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the lack of Hermitian conjugation between left and right eigenvectors.
method: The authors propose a covariant approach to define the Berry connection and curvature that is independent of the choice of biorthogonal basis, using a gauge-invariant formalism.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the covariant Berry connection and demonstrate its application to simple non-Hermitian models, showing consistency with known topological invariants.
conclusion: The covariant formulation resolves the ambiguity in geometric phases for non-Hermitian systems and provides a robust framework for studying their topology.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum neural networks preserve plasticity in continual learning, unlike classical networks.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and the authors investigate whether quantum neural networks can overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the parameter evolution of quantum neural networks during sequential task learning and demonstrate intrinsic preservation of plasticity.
result: Quantum neural networks maintain the ability to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones due to the structure of unitary evolution.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks offer a natural advantage for continual learning, which could be useful for adaptive quantum machine learning systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and efficient approach.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to build a configurable photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates that a wide class of quantum field theories can be simulated with high efficiency and configurability using photonic hardware.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator provides a practical platform for studying quantum field dynamics, with potential applications in quantum simulation.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, identifying depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and replica methods, to derive universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise rate.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits three depth-dependent regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a saturation regime. The universal regime is independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: The results provide a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which is relevant for assessing the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and for benchmarking noisy quantum devices.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct information-theoretic results.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity for various matrix functions, highlighting potential quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work offers insights into quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but its contribution is more about complexity classification than core quantum information theory.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verification, but existing methods struggle with large multiqubit unitaries. The authors aim to extend the reach of stabilizer-based simulation by leveraging symmetries.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for larger systems, building on the Gottesman-Knill theorem and Clifford circuit simulation.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reduction significantly improves the efficiency of classical simulation for Clifford-dominated circuits, enabling the simulation of circuits beyond previous limits.
conclusion: Symmetry-accelerated stabilizer decompositions provide a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, with potential applications in quantum circuit verification and benchmarking.

title: Composite-dimensional Topological Codes With Boundaries And Defects
authors: Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, And Eugene Dumitrescu
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, and Eugene Dumitrescu

We introduce new algorithms and provide example constructions of stabilizer models for the gapped boundaries, domain walls, and [MATH] defects of Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles. Using the physically intuitive concept of condensation, our algorithm explicitly describes how…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012438] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces algorithms and constructions for stabilizer models of gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
motivation: Topological codes with boundaries and defects are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but composite-dimensional codes have been less explored.
method: The authors use the concept of condensation to algorithmically describe boundaries, domain walls, and defects, and provide explicit stabilizer constructions.
result: New algorithms and example stabilizer models for composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles are presented.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of topological codes to composite dimensions, potentially enabling more flexible fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Thermodynamic Constraints On Perfect Equilibrium Superconducting Diodes
authors: Pavan Hosur
abstract:
Author(s): Pavan Hosur

Why are perfect superconducting diodes so elusive? Here, the author shows that near-perfect diode behavior requires singularities in the equilibrium free energy landscape. This explains why high efficiencies arise more naturally in engineered Josephson devices and predicts that unexpectedly large efficiencies in equilibrium superconductors imply hidden structure in the free energy landscape.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020505] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that perfect superconducting diodes require singularities in the equilibrium free energy landscape, explaining why high efficiencies are rare in equilibrium systems.
motivation: Superconducting diodes are highly sought for applications, but perfect efficiency is elusive; the author seeks a thermodynamic explanation for this difficulty.
method: The author analyzes the equilibrium free energy landscape of superconducting diodes, deriving necessary conditions for perfect diode behavior.
result: Near-perfect diode behavior requires singularities in the free energy landscape, which are rare in equilibrium systems, explaining why high efficiencies are more common in engineered Josephson devices.
conclusion: The findings predict that unexpectedly large efficiencies in equilibrium superconductors imply hidden structure in the free energy landscape.

title: Critical States Preparation In Light-matter Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan Xia

The fast and efficient preparation of quantum critical states is a challenging yet crucial task for various quantum technologies. This difficulty is most particularly for systems near a quantum phase transition, where the closure of the energy gap fundamentally limits the timescale of adiabatic proc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033063] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: Uses deep reinforcement learning to prepare quantum critical states in light-matter systems near a quantum phase transition.
motivation: Fast and efficient preparation of quantum critical states is challenging due to the closure of the energy gap near phase transitions, limiting adiabatic methods.
method: Applies deep reinforcement learning to design control pulses that drive the system into critical states, bypassing adiabatic constraints.
result: Demonstrates faster and more robust preparation of critical states compared to traditional adiabatic protocols.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical approach for preparing critical states, with potential applications in quantum simulation and metrology.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging because logical gates often require braiding of anyons, which is limited in planar architectures.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform complex logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding.
result: They demonstrate that universal fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in 2D without braiding, using a new approach based on non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: This work provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation in two-dimensional systems.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to parallelize the process.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to traditional magic state distillation protocols.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy with low latency, enabling real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error patterns, using a heuristic to prune the search space and achieve near-optimal decoding performance.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy comparable to maximum-likelihood decoding while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, without requiring massive classical resources.
conclusion: Beam search decoding is a practical solution for quantum LDPC codes, enabling efficient and fast error correction for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a 'just-in-time' decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementations of non-Clifford gates, which are challenging on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and they propose a 'just-in-time' decoder to handle errors.
result: The circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance with the proposed decoder, demonstrating a practical approach for universal quantum computing on planar chips.
conclusion: This work provides a concrete circuit design for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the color code, advancing the feasibility of planar quantum computing architectures.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates (T-count) is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation because T gates are costly to implement with error correction. The paper aims to leverage commuting structures to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli operators to be commuted through T gates simultaneously, enabling more efficient circuit compilation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces T-count compared to existing methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits, potentially lowering the resource overhead for quantum algorithms.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need to characterize Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define and quantify Majorana bound states in interacting systems, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models to compute robustness and locality measures.
result: They provide quantitative criteria for the protection of Majorana bound states and evaluate their suitability for non-Abelian braiding in the presence of interactions.
conclusion: The work offers a rigorous characterization of Majorana bound states in interacting systems, which is important for assessing their potential in topological quantum computing but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in hybrid quantum systems or quantum information thermodynamics.

title: Ellipticity-Controlled Bright-Dark Coherence Transition In Monolayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$
authors: Kang Lan, Xiangji Cai, Zhongxiao Man, Shijie Xie, Ning Hao, Ping Zhang, And Jiyong Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Lan, Xiangji Cai, Zhongxiao Man, Shijie Xie, Ning Hao, Ping Zhang, and Jiyong Fu

The generation of exciton valley coherence typically requires linearly polarized (LP) light as an external coherent drive, whereas circularly polarized (CP) light fails to induce coherence. Here, we develop a unified, microscopically grounded open-quantum-system framework within a five-level model i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036202] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ellipticity-controlled bright-dark coherence transition in monolayer WSe2 using an open quantum system framework.
motivation: Understanding and controlling exciton valley coherence in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for valleytronics and quantum information applications.
method: The authors develop a five-level open quantum system model to describe the dynamics of exciton states under elliptically polarized light, incorporating bright and dark exciton states and their coupling to phonons.
result: They find that the ellipticity of the driving laser can control the transition from bright to dark exciton coherence, with a critical ellipticity where coherence vanishes.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic understanding of valley coherence control, which may enable new optoelectronic and quantum devices based on valley degrees of freedom.

title: Signatures Of Infinite Randomness In Transport Properties Of Strongly Disordered Spin Chains
authors: L. F. C. Faria, Victor L. Quito, João C. Getelina, José A. Hoyos, And E. Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): L. F. C. Faria, Victor L. Quito, João C. Getelina, José A. Hoyos, and E. Miranda

We study the spin transport properties of some disordered spin chains with a special focus on the distribution of the frequency-dependent spin conductivity. In the cases of interest here, the systems are governed by an effectively infinite disorder at low energies. A hallmark of this behavior is the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014206] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin transport in strongly disordered spin chains, focusing on the distribution of frequency-dependent spin conductivity and signatures of infinite randomness.
motivation: Understanding transport in disordered quantum systems is important for many-body localization and quantum thermodynamics, but the paper's focus on spin conductivity in disordered chains is not directly aligned with the core interests.
method: The authors analyze spin transport properties using theoretical and numerical methods, examining the distribution of spin conductivity in the presence of strong disorder.
result: They identify signatures of infinite randomness in the transport properties, such as broad distributions of conductivity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into disordered spin chains but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:
Author(s): M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, and M. Eisenbach

Quantum embedding methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), provide a powerful framework for investigating strongly correlated materials. A central computational bottleneck in DMFT is in solving the Anderson impurity model (AIM), whose exact solution is classically intractable for large b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033066] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to solve the single-impurity Anderson model with particle-hole symmetry on a quantum computer, aiming to accelerate DMFT calculations for strongly correlated materials.
motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is a computational bottleneck in DMFT, and classical methods become intractable for large bath sizes. A quantum solver could enable more accurate simulations of strongly correlated materials.
method: The authors design a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) tailored to the Anderson impurity model with particle-hole symmetry, using a specific ansatz and measurement scheme to compute the ground state and Green's function.
result: Numerical simulations show that the quantum solver can reproduce exact results for small system sizes, and resource estimates suggest feasibility for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: The proposed quantum algorithm offers a potential path to overcome classical limitations in DMFT, but experimental demonstration and scaling to larger systems remain challenges.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires large overhead in qubits and time; this work aims to reduce both using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques with good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may reveal novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving mechanisms.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the statistical geometry of active repulsive rods and disks, showing that activity increases insertion volume and connectivity.
motivation: Understanding how active motion affects the geometry of available space in repulsive systems is important for statistical physics of active matter.
method: The authors combine theoretical analysis and simulations to compute insertion volume and surface area for active hard rods and disks.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the statistical geometry of repulsive systems, which may have implications for packing and transport in active matter.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:
Author(s): Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, and Yoshinobu Kawahara

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution.
motivation: Neural quantum state architectures are often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated design principle.
method: They introduce a framework where NQS are viewed as neural approximations to imaginary-time evolution, using a latent space and a variational Monte Carlo approach.
result: The framework yields competitive ground-state energies for spin models and offers interpretability through the latent dynamics.
conclusion: The approach bridges machine learning and quantum many-body physics, but the contribution is primarily methodological and not directly advancing quantum information theory.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Belief propagation is a heuristic for tensor network contraction that lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to provide systematic corrections with provable convergence.
method: The authors develop a cluster expansion approach that adds corrections to belief propagation, leading to a polynomial-time algorithm with exponential convergence in the cluster size.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence of approximation errors, with rigorous bounds, and is demonstrated on various tensor networks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected belief propagation offers a practical and provably accurate method for tensor network contraction, bridging heuristic and rigorous approaches.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian topology in a tunable dissipative many-body system, which is a topic in condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A cold Rydberg gas is used as a dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: Interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity are observed.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for studying non-Hermitian topology but does not directly contribute to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: The algorithm achieves provable exponential speedup over classical methods for certain instances, as shown by complexity analysis.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, but the relevance to quantum information theory is limited.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is believed to be a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating scalability.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their relation to quantum computation.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach by treating space and time on the same footing.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution in lattice systems leads to brickwork quantum circuits, and explores the intrinsic relationship between space-time duality and these circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality, highlighting connections to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful framework for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep links to quantum circuit models.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent work connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover reproducible behaviors in neural data, demonstrating predictive power similar to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical principles, advancing our understanding of brain function.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, and Jian-Wei Pan

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns and short-range correlations in fermionic Hubbard gases after ballistic expansion from optical lattices.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems is important, and interference patterns provide information about phase coherence and nonlocal correlations.
method: The authors experimentally observe interference of ultracold fermionic atoms released from optical lattices and analyze the resulting patterns.
result: They extract signatures of short-range correlations and phase coherence in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that interference of fermionic gases can reveal correlation properties, extending techniques previously applied to bosons.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space-group pairs.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify whether chirality can be ferroic.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, as it does not satisfy the necessary symmetry conditions for a ferroic order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality should not be classified as a ferroic property, which has implications for the understanding of chiral materials and their phase transitions.

title: Antiferromagnetism And Stripe Channel Order In The $\mathrm{SU}(N)$-Symmetric Two-Channel Kondo Lattice Model
authors: Elyasaf Y. Cohen, Fakher F. Assaad, And Snir Gazit
abstract:
Author(s): Elyasaf Y. Cohen, Fakher F. Assaad, and Snir Gazit

We carry out large-scale, sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the square lattice [MATH]-symmetric two-channel Kondo lattice model at half-filling. We map out the zero-temperature phase diagram for [MATH], 4, 6, and 8, as a function of the Kondo coupling strength…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036504] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of an SU(N)-symmetric two-channel Kondo lattice model using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, focusing on antiferromagnetism and stripe channel order.
motivation: To understand the interplay between Kondo screening and magnetic ordering in multi-channel Kondo lattice models, which are relevant to heavy-fermion materials.
method: Large-scale, sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations on a square lattice at half-filling for various N and Kondo coupling strengths.
result: Maps out the zero-temperature phase diagram, revealing antiferromagnetic and stripe channel ordered phases depending on N and coupling.
conclusion: The model exhibits rich magnetic and channel ordering, providing insights into correlated electron systems with SU(N) symmetry.

title: Spin-Triplet Paired Wigner Crystal Stabilized By Quantum Geometry
authors: Dmitry Zverevich, Alex Levchenko, And Ilya Esterlis

We have used variational states to analyze the effects of band geometry on the two-dimensional Wigner crystal with one and two electrons per unit cell. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036506] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a spin-triplet paired Wigner crystal stabilized by quantum geometry in a two-dimensional electron system.
motivation: To understand the effects of band geometry and Berry curvature on the Wigner crystal phase at low electron densities.
method: Variational wavefunction analysis for Wigner crystals with one and two electrons per unit cell, incorporating Berry curvature effects.
result: Increasing Berry curvature drives a transition to a crystalline state composed of spin-triplet pairs.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can stabilize novel paired crystalline phases in low-density electron systems.

title: Harnessing Spin-Texture Dynamics For Low-Noise, High-Sensitivity Magnetic Sensors

The development of low-noise, high-sensitivity magnetic sensors is essential for applications such as automotive systems, biomedical imaging, and magnetic microscopy. However, sensor performance has long been impeded by a fundamental constraint that noise and sensitivity increase concomitantly, whic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036705] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to break the noise-sensitivity trade-off in magnetic sensors by exploiting spin-texture dynamics.
motivation: Magnetic sensors are limited by a fundamental trade-off between noise and sensitivity; the authors aim to overcome this constraint.
method: They utilize spin-texture dynamics, likely involving skyrmions or domain walls, to achieve simultaneous low noise and high sensitivity.
result: The proposed sensor demonstrates improved performance, breaking the conventional trade-off.
conclusion: Spin-texture dynamics offer a promising route for next-generation magnetic sensors.

title: Synchronization Driven Reciprocity Breaking
authors: Alexander K. Stoychev, Ulrich Kuhl, And Nicolas Noiray
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander K. Stoychev, Ulrich Kuhl, and Nicolas Noiray

Wave transmission reciprocity is broken by exploiting the synchronization of two coupled self-oscillators. The underlying principle is that illumination from one port drives the in phase, while illumination from the other port drives the antiphase synchronization state. Because of its self-adjustmen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033802] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates non-reciprocal wave transmission by exploiting synchronization of coupled self-oscillators.
motivation: To achieve reciprocity breaking in wave transmission without external magnetic fields or nonlinearities, using a self-adjusting mechanism.
method: Two coupled self-oscillators are driven from opposite ports, leading to in-phase or anti-phase synchronization depending on the illumination direction.
result: The system exhibits direction-dependent transmission, breaking reciprocity through synchronization dynamics.
conclusion: Synchronization-driven reciprocity breaking offers a new approach for non-reciprocal devices, with potential applications in acoustics and photonics.

tldr: This paper studies the microwave signature of the emerging Abrikosov lattice in type-II superconducting films above the upper critical field.
motivation: To understand the precursor effects of vortex lattice formation in the normal phase of superconductors, which is a fundamental aspect of condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of microwave conductivity fluctuations to predict a signature of the Abrikosov lattice above H_c2.
result: They find that the microwave response exhibits a characteristic feature indicating the onset of vortex lattice order even above the critical field.
conclusion: The work provides a way to detect vortex lattice fluctuations in the normal state, but it is focused on superconducting physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Microscopic Evidence For A Zhang-Rice Triplet State In The Van Der Waals Antiferromagnet, ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$

tldr: This paper uses NMR to verify a Zhang-Rice triplet ground state in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS3.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ground state of NiPS3, a candidate for two-dimensional magnetism.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on single crystals of NiPS3.
result: Evidence for a Zhang-Rice triplet state, confirming the triplet ground state.
conclusion: The Zhang-Rice triplet state is the correct description of the magnetic properties of NiPS3.

title: Photoinduced Switching Of Magnetization In The Epsilon-Near-Zero Regime
authors: Héloïse Damas, Carl S. Davies, Petr M. Vetoshko, Vladimir I. Belotelov, Andrzej Stupakiewicz, And Andrei Kirilyuk

Midinfrared laser pulses tuned to optical phonon frequencies can induce magnetization switching in magnetic dielectrics, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear, since excitations of the crystal lattice can simultaneously produce heating and nonthermal strain. Here, we study the response of lab…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036704] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced magnetization switching in magnetic dielectrics using midinfrared laser pulses tuned to optical phonon frequencies.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms behind ultrafast magnetization switching is important for spintronics and data storage, but the role of lattice excitations and nonthermal strain remains unclear.
method: The authors experimentally investigate the response of a magnetic dielectric to midinfrared laser pulses in the epsilon-near-zero regime, analyzing the contributions of heating and nonthermal strain.
result: They observe magnetization switching and characterize the underlying dynamics, distinguishing thermal and nonthermal effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into photoinduced magnetization switching, but the work is primarily experimental and focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Directional Photocurrent Generated By Quantum Interference Control
authors: Yiming Gong, Kai Wang, And Steven T. Cundiff
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Gong, Kai Wang, and Steven T. Cundiff

Using higher-order quantum interference, an “electron lighthouse” is created with the capability of optically steering highly directional 2D beams of photocurrent in semiconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036901] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate highly directional photocurrent in semiconductors using higher-order quantum interference.
motivation: To achieve optical steering of photocurrent beams for potential applications in optoelectronics and photonics.
method: Using higher-order quantum interference control with tailored optical pulses to create an 'electron lighthouse' effect.
result: Directional 2D beams of photocurrent are generated and steered optically in semiconductors.
conclusion: Quantum interference control can be used to create steerable photocurrent beams, which may have applications in ultrafast optoelectronics.

title: Optical Soliton Cooper Pairs In Mamyshev Oscillators
