The framework of superconductivity unveiled the striking concept that electrons form Cooper pairs through the subtle interplay of lattice vibrations, surmounting their Coulombic repulsion in the process. The concept of Cooper pairs has been established beyond the Fermi system, and this pairing mecha…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033801] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optical analog of Cooper pairs using solitons in Mamyshev oscillators, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore the concept of Cooper pairing beyond Fermi systems and demonstrate it in a classical optical system.
method: The authors theoretically model and experimentally demonstrate soliton pairs in a Mamyshev oscillator, drawing an analogy to Cooper pairs in superconductivity.
result: They observe stable soliton pairs that exhibit binding energy and pairing behavior analogous to Cooper pairs.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of Cooper pairing to classical nonlinear optics, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superradiant Parametric Mössbauer Radiation Source

motivation: Future applications of Mössbauer nuclei require x-ray sources with exceptionally high peak and average spectral flux, which current sources cannot provide.
method: The authors introduce a scheme utilizing scattering of spatially microstructured electron beams from Mössbauer nuclei to achieve superradiant parametric emission.
result: The proposed source achieves high spectral flux and narrow linewidth, suitable for Mössbauer spectroscopy.
conclusion: The SPMR source offers a promising approach for advanced x-ray applications in nuclear quantum optics.

title: Kondo Effect In Nonreciprocal Response
authors: Hajime Murata And Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract:

Chiral magnetic states give rise to rich phenomena, from the anomalous Hall effect and the nonlinear electrical current to multiferroics and magnetochiral dichroism. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036301] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect in nonreciprocal transport, focusing on chiral magnetic states and nonlinear electrical response.
motivation: To understand how magnetic moments in chiral magnets affect electrical transport beyond linear response.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Kondo effect in a nonreciprocal setting, likely using perturbation theory or numerical methods.
result: They find that nonreciprocal response arises from the interplay of Kondo screening and chirality.
conclusion: The work reveals a new aspect of Kondo physics in chiral systems, relevant for spintronics and nonlinear transport.

title: Nonlinear Odd Viscoelastic Effect
authors: Ashwat Jain, Wojciech J. Jankowski, M. Mehraeen, And Robert-Jan Slager

motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum geometry and viscoelastic response in topological materials.
method: Theoretical analysis using higher-order quantum geometric tensors and response theory for distortion fields.
result: Prediction of nonlinear odd viscoelastic effects in magnetic three-dimensional topological phases.
conclusion: Quantum geometric tensors can lead to novel viscoelastic phenomena in topological materials.

title: Even Denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States In The Zeroth Landau Level Of Aba Trilayer Graphene
authors: Tanima Chanda, Simrandeep Kaur, Harsimran Singh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Manish Jain, Udit Khanna, Ajit C. Balram, And Aveek Bid

Even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at half-filling are of particular interest because they can host non-Abelian quasiparticles. Here, we report the emergence of such states in the zeroth Landau level ([MATH]) of ABA trilayer graphene (TLG), challenging the conventional expectation that t…

tldr: This paper reports the observation of even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states in the zeroth Landau level of ABA trilayer graphene, which are of interest for hosting non-Abelian quasiparticles.
motivation: Even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states are candidates for non-Abelian anyons, which are important for topological quantum computation. The zeroth Landau level in trilayer graphene was previously thought to not support such states.
method: The authors performed transport measurements on ABA trilayer graphene devices at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, identifying fractional quantum Hall states by their quantized Hall conductance.
result: They observed even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at filling factors such as 1/2 and 3/2 in the zeroth Landau level, challenging previous theoretical expectations.
conclusion: The discovery opens new possibilities for studying non-Abelian quasiparticles in graphene-based systems, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Demonstration Of Deuterium’s Enhanced Sensitivity To Symmetry Violations Governed By The Standard-Model Extension

Several nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model extensi…

tldr: This paper reports hyperfine spectroscopy of deuterium to search for Lorentz and CPT violation using the Standard-Model Extension.
motivation: To test fundamental symmetries (Lorentz and CPT) by looking for sidereal variations in deuterium hyperfine transitions.
method: Hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium, analyzing data for sidereal variations to constrain nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.
result: No evidence of Lorentz or CPT violation was found, setting improved constraints on certain SME coefficients.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates enhanced sensitivity to symmetry violations in deuterium but does not directly advance the user's research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Commensurate-Incommensurate Mott Transition Without Magnetic Field: Emergence Of Nematic Luttinger Liquid In Xxz Chain

tldr: This paper studies the zero-magnetization ground state phase diagram of a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, revealing a nematic Luttinger liquid phase.
motivation: To understand the emergence of nematic order and commensurate-incommensurate transitions in quantum spin chains without an external magnetic field.

result: A nematic Luttinger liquid phase is found, and the commensurate-incommensurate Mott transition is characterized.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exotic quantum phases in frustrated spin chains, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pseudochiral Phonons From Octupolar Magnetic Order
authors: Ruairidh Sutcliffe, Kathleen Hart, Swati Chaudhary, And Arun Paramekanti

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036703] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces pseudochiral phonons in multipolar magnets, focusing on a condensed matter phenomenon without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Recent discovery of large magnetic response of chiral phonons in dipolar magnets motivates exploring similar effects in multipolar magnets.
method: The authors theoretically analyze Raman active quantum phonons in multipolar magnets, introducing the concept of pseudochiral phonons.
result: They show that pseudochiral phonons emerge in multipolar magnets, analogous to chiral phonons in dipolar magnets.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of phonon-magnetism coupling to multipolar systems, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh
abstract:

We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful dynamical probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013314] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate after a sudden change in polarization direction.
motivation: To probe superfluid and solid-like properties of dipolar BECs using a sudden change in magnetic dipole polarization direction.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of a dipolar BEC after a sudden rotation of the polarization direction, calculating the resulting density and phase evolution.
result: They find that the dynamical response exhibits distinct signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity depending on the phase of the condensate.

title: Electric Dipole Spin-flip Resonances In Semiconductors: A Personal Perspective
authors: Bruce D. Mccombe
abstract:
Author(s): Bruce D. McCombe

Emmanuel Rashba is responsible for a body of theory that demonstrates the profound effects of spin-orbit interaction on charge carriers in semiconductors. This notably includes the discovery of important effects on confined carriers in the presence of structural inversion asymmetry. The present article describes, from a personal perspective, experimental discovery and studies of electric-field-excited spin-flip resonances in semiconductors motivated by these theoretical predictions. Initial experiments in 1960 focused on electric-dipole excited spin resonance (EDSR) and combined cyclotron plus spin resonance (in 1967). Recent experiments on quasi-two-dimensional electrons in the quantum Hall effect regime in an asymmetric quantum-well structure have revealed unusual multiline EDSR spectra attributed to effects of Rashba spin-orbit effective fields of electrons in quantum Hall edge channels.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019603] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A personal perspective on experimental discovery of electric-dipole spin-flip resonances in semiconductors, motivated by Rashba's theory.
motivation: To provide a historical account of electric-field-excited spin-flip resonances in semiconductors, driven by Rashba's predictions on spin-orbit interaction effects.
method: Review of experimental studies from 1960 onward, including electric-dipole excited spin resonance (EDSR) and combined cyclotron plus spin resonance, with recent experiments on quasi-2D electrons in asymmetric quantum wells.
result: Discovery of unusual multiline EDSR spectra attributed to Rashba spin-orbit effective fields in quantum Hall edge channels.
conclusion: The work highlights the lasting impact of Rashba's theory on experimental semiconductor physics, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

Author(s): Maximilian Buthenhoff and Yusuke Nishida

By coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory with isolated bands to an external gravitomagnetic vector potential via a gravitomagnetic Peierls substitution, we identify a quantum-geometric contribution to the electronic contribution of the thermal conductivity. This contribution is governed by…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024508] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a quantum-geometric contribution to thermal conductivity in superconductors using BCS theory and a gravitomagnetic Peierls substitution.
motivation: To understand the role of quantum geometry in transport properties of superconductors beyond conventional BCS theory.
method: Couples BCS theory with isolated bands to an external gravitomagnetic vector potential via a gravitomagnetic Peierls substitution.
result: Identifies a quantum-geometric contribution to the electronic thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can influence thermal transport in superconductors, providing a new perspective on thermal conductivity.

title: Observation Of $π/3$ And $2π/3$ Modes In An Acoustic Floquet System
authors: Zheng-Bo Cheng, Hong-Xiang Sun, Shou-Qi Yuan, Zheyu Cheng, And Baile Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng-bo Cheng, Hong-xiang Sun, Shou-qi Yuan, Zheyu Cheng, and Baile Zhang

Floquet topological systems support boundary states pinned at discrete quasienergies. Here, the authors experimentally realize Floquet edge states with fractional quasienergies /3 and /3 in an acoustic waveguide array, establishing a new family of fractional Floquet edge states beyond the conventional 0 and
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034207] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of fractional Floquet edge states at π/3 and 2π/3 quasienergies in an acoustic waveguide array.
motivation: To demonstrate the existence of fractional Floquet edge states beyond the conventional 0 and π quasienergy modes.
method: Acoustic waveguide array with periodic driving, measuring edge state dispersion via transmission spectra.
result: Observation of edge states pinned at π/3 and 2π/3 quasienergies, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Establishes a new family of fractional Floquet edge states, expanding the understanding of topological phases in driven systems.

title: Probing Floquet Topological Phases Via non-Hermitian Skin Effect Of Reflected Waves
authors: Fangqiao Ye And Haiping Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangqiao Ye and Haiping Hu

Here, the authors theoretically propose an approach to probe Floquet topological phases utilizing the non-Hermitian skin effect of reflected waves. They demonstrate that in periodically driven systems, unique topological signatures are robustly encoded in the reflection signals at the boundaries. This work provides a practical framework for experimentally identifying nonequilibrium topological phenomena without needing bulk measurements.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034310] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes probing Floquet topological phases via the non-Hermitian skin effect of reflected waves.
motivation: To develop a practical method for identifying nonequilibrium topological phenomena without bulk measurements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze reflection signals at boundaries of periodically driven systems, showing that topological signatures are encoded in the non-Hermitian skin effect of reflected waves.
result: Unique topological signatures are robustly encoded in reflection signals, providing a framework for experimental identification.
conclusion: This work offers a practical approach to probe Floquet topological phases using boundary reflection measurements.

title: Coexisting Paramagnetic Spins And Long-range Magnetic Order In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{4}{({\mathrm{Ru}}_{0.92}{\mathrm{Ir}}_{0.08})}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Farhan Islam, Jiasen Guo, Wei Tian, Bing Li, Xudong Huai, Thao T. Tran, Gang Cao, Zachary Morgan, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Farhan Islam, Jiasen Guo, Wei Tian, Bing Li, Xudong Huai, Thao T. Tran, Gang Cao, Zachary Morgan, and Feng Ye

We investigate the effect of dilute Ir substitution on the magnetism of the trimer-based ruthenate [MATH] using neutron diffraction, magnetic susceptibility measurements, first-principles calculations, and atomistic simulations. Neutron diffraction show…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034416] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a ruthenate material with dilute iridium substitution, focusing on the coexistence of paramagnetic spins and long-range magnetic order.
motivation: To understand how dilute Ir substitution affects the magnetism of trimer-based ruthenates, which may reveal novel magnetic phases.
method: Neutron diffraction, magnetic susceptibility measurements, first-principles calculations, and atomistic simulations.
result: Coexistence of paramagnetic spins and long-range magnetic order is observed, with Ir substitution modifying the magnetic interactions.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic behavior of doped ruthenates, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Toward A Unified Description Of Valley Polarization In Two-dimensional Tetragonal Altermagnets Driven By Strain And In-plane Magnetization
authors: Bo Huang, Churen Gui, Ao Zhang, Zhixiong Yang, Shu-Zong Li, Zhenqing Li, Hongxing Li, And Wei-Bing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Huang, Churen Gui, Ao Zhang, Zhixiong Yang, Shu-Zong Li, Zhenqing Li, Hongxing Li, and Wei-Bing Zhang

Altermagnetism provides a promising platform for valleytronics applications due to its symmetry-protected spin-valley locking. While uniaxial strain and in-plane magnetization have recently emerged as novel routes to induce valley polarization in altermagnets, a unified theoretical framework elucida…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045421] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley polarization in two-dimensional tetragonal altermagnets driven by strain and in-plane magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for valleytronics, but a unified theoretical framework for valley polarization induced by strain and magnetization is lacking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to describe valley polarization in tetragonal altermagnets.
result: They find that both uniaxial strain and in-plane magnetization can induce valley polarization, and they provide a unified description of the underlying mechanisms.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of valley control in altermagnets, which may benefit valleytronic applications.

title: Reverse Design Of Topological Metamaterials Based On Tight-binding Models
authors: Mingze Weng, Maopeng Wu, Siyong Zheng, Fubei Liu, Qian Zhao, Yonggang Meng, And Ji Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Weng, Maopeng Wu, Siyong Zheng, Fubei Liu, Qian Zhao, Yonggang Meng, and Ji Zhou

Metamaterials provide a versatile platform for realizing topological phases and exploring non-Hermitian physics. However, the design of metamaterials exhibiting such rich physics is challenging because conventional design approaches require constant iterative optimization, which unfortunately is bot…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055120] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a reverse design method for topological metamaterials using tight-binding models and deep learning.
motivation: Conventional design of topological metamaterials requires iterative optimization and is inefficient; a reverse design approach is needed.
method: The authors use a deep neural network to map target topological properties (e.g., band topology) to tight-binding model parameters, enabling inverse design.
result: The method successfully generates metamaterial designs with desired topological phases, including non-Hermitian effects.
conclusion: Reverse design based on tight-binding models can efficiently produce topological metamaterials, bypassing traditional trial-and-error.

title: Theory Of Next-generation Even-denominator States
authors: Misha Yutushui And David F. Mross
abstract:
Author(s): Misha Yutushui and David F. Mross

Here, the authors establish a comprehensive theory for the recently observed “next-generation” even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states and reveal that they are topologically equivalent to Bonderson-Slingerland phases. They present numerical simulations showing significant and systematic microscopic differences between the two families of states: next-generation states are favored in the lowest Landau level, while Bonderson-Slingerland states are favored in the first excited level. Finally, the authors prove that essential universal properties of topological edges are preserved under flux attachment and leverage this result to predict experimental signatures of next-generation even-denominator states.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065121] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory for next-generation even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states, showing they are topologically equivalent to Bonderson-Slingerland phases but with different microscopic origins.
motivation: Recent experiments observed new even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states that do not fit existing theories, motivating a comprehensive theoretical understanding.
method: The authors use topological field theory, flux attachment, and numerical simulations to compare next-generation states with Bonderson-Slingerland states.
result: Next-generation states are favored in the lowest Landau level, while Bonderson-Slingerland states are favored in the first excited level; essential universal properties of topological edges are preserved under flux attachment.
conclusion: Next-generation even-denominator states are topologically equivalent to Bonderson-Slingerland phases but have distinct microscopic origins, leading to different experimental signatures.

title: Effective Long-range Attraction Of Moiré Excitons Under The Influence Of Atomic Reconstructions And Anisotropic Screening
authors: Nils-Erik Schütte, Carl Emil Mørch Nielsen, Niclas Götting, Alexander Steinhoff, Gabriel Bester, And Christopher Gies
abstract:
Author(s): Nils-Erik Schütte, Carl Emil Mørch Nielsen, Niclas Götting, Alexander Steinhoff, Gabriel Bester, and Christopher Gies

The moiré pattern, which emerges due to a relative rotation between two monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides, features a long lattice period for small twist angles. The resulting band-structure modulation acts as an effective potential for interlayer excitons, which can realize correlated …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065417] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effective long-range attraction of moiré excitons in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers, focusing on atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening.
motivation: Understanding the interaction between moiré excitons is crucial for realizing correlated quantum phases, but the role of atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening has been unclear.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening to compute the effective potential between interlayer excitons in twisted TMDs.
result: They find that atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening lead to an effective long-range attraction between moiré excitons, which can stabilize correlated states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exciton interactions in moiré systems, relevant for engineering quantum phases in TMD heterostructures.

title: Generalized Framework Of Ferroelectric Controlled Nonlinear Hall Effect Driven By Berry Curvature Dipole
authors: Zhenyu Lu, Xiaoliang Xiao, Xingyu Yue, Jin-Zhu Zhao, Rui-Chun Xiao, And Yuanjun Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Lu, Xiaoliang Xiao, Xingyu Yue, Jin-Zhu Zhao, Rui-Chun Xiao, and Yuanjun Jin

The nonlinear Hall effect has emerged as an essential field in condensed matter physics for its connection with the properties of quantum geometry and its potential application in electronic devices. However, when the nonlinear Hall current scales quadratically with a single driving electric field, …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014104] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonlinear Hall effect driven by Berry curvature dipole in ferroelectric materials, focusing on condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear Hall effect in ferroelectric systems and its connection to quantum geometry for potential electronic device applications.
method: The authors develop a generalized theoretical framework based on Berry curvature dipole and apply it to ferroelectric materials.
result: They find that ferroelectric control can modulate the nonlinear Hall effect, revealing new features driven by Berry curvature dipole.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for engineering nonlinear Hall effects in ferroelectric materials, relevant for device applications.

title: Long-range Machine-learning Potentials With Environment-dependent Charges Enable Predicting Lo-to Splitting And Dielectric Constants
authors: Dmitry Korogod, Alexander V. Shapeev, And Ivan S. Novikov
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitry Korogod, Alexander V. Shapeev, and Ivan S. Novikov

We present two models with explicit long-range electrostatics in the form of Coulomb interactions. Both models include point charges depending on their local atomic environments, and the second model also conserves a total charge of an atomic system. We combine the proposed long-range models with th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024104] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops machine learning potentials with environment-dependent charges to model long-range electrostatics in materials, focusing on predicting LO-TO splitting and dielectric constants.
motivation: Accurate modeling of long-range electrostatic interactions is crucial for predicting properties of polar materials, but traditional methods are computationally expensive.
method: Two models are proposed: one with environment-dependent point charges and another that additionally conserves total charge, combined with a short-range machine learning potential.
result: The models successfully predict LO-TO splitting and dielectric constants for a range of materials, demonstrating improved accuracy over standard approaches.
conclusion: The proposed machine learning potentials with explicit long-range electrostatics offer an efficient and accurate way to compute dielectric properties of materials.

title: Lattice And $\mathcal{PT}$ Symmetries In Tensor-network Renormalization Group: Case Study Of A Hard-square Lattice Gas Model
authors: Xinliang Lyu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinliang Lyu

The tensor-network renormalization group (TNRG) is an accurate numerical real-space renormalization group method for studying phase transitions in both quantum and classical systems. Continuous phase transitions, as an important class of phase transitions, are usually accompanied by spontaneous brea…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034111] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies tensor-network renormalization group to study phase transitions in a hard-square lattice gas model, focusing on lattice and PT symmetries.
motivation: To accurately compute critical exponents and understand the role of symmetries in tensor-network renormalization group methods.
method: Uses tensor-network renormalization group (TNRG) with explicit handling of lattice and PT symmetries to analyze the hard-square lattice gas model.
result: Obtains critical exponents and phase transition properties, demonstrating the effectiveness of symmetry-preserving TNRG.
conclusion: The symmetry-preserving TNRG approach yields accurate results for classical statistical models with discrete symmetries.

title: Pseudogap And Strange Metal States In The Square-lattice Hubbard Model: A Comprehensive Study
authors: Arata Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Arata Tanaka

To clarify the origin of the pseudogap and strange metal states as well as their mutual relationship in cuprate superconductors, a comprehensive study on the spectral function, Fermi surface, resistivity, and dynamical spin susceptivity of the Hubbard model on the square lattice has been conducted b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045114] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pseudogap and strange metal states in the square-lattice Hubbard model, focusing on cuprate superconductors.
motivation: To clarify the origin of the pseudogap and strange metal states and their relationship in cuprate superconductors.
method: Comprehensive study using spectral function, Fermi surface, resistivity, and dynamical spin susceptibility calculations on the Hubbard model.
result: The paper provides detailed analysis of the pseudogap and strange metal phases, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
conclusion: The findings contribute to condensed matter physics but are not aligned with the specified research interests.

title: Origin Of Acceptor Preference In Silicon, Diamond, And Silicon Carbide
authors: Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, And Su-Huai Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, and Su-Huai Wei

Silicon, diamond, and their compound silicon carbide play pivotal roles in electronic science and technology. Trivalent impurities such as B and Al are the typical choices for [MATH]-type doping in these semiconductors. Intriguingly, B dominates in Si and diamond, while Al is preferred in SiC for indus…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045203] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of acceptor preference (B vs Al) in silicon, diamond, and silicon carbide semiconductors using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Understanding why B is preferred in Si and diamond while Al is preferred in SiC is important for optimizing p-type doping in these technologically crucial semiconductors.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) were performed to compute formation energies and electronic structures of B and Al dopants in Si, diamond, and SiC.
result: The preference is explained by differences in atomic size, electronegativity, and lattice relaxation effects, with B being more stable in Si and diamond due to smaller size mismatch, while Al is favored in SiC due to better bond strength and reduced strain.
conclusion: The study provides a fundamental understanding of dopant selection in group-IV semiconductors, guiding future doping strategies for electronic devices.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper shows that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a standard model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) rotational symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to demonstrate the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the model's order parameter does not correspond to a broken continuous symmetry, and the phase transition is not associated with O(2) symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect; the model's phase transition has a different origin.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of the fractional derivative order.
conclusion: The work provides analytical results for a class of superdiffusive processes, but its relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: Finding optimal paths in fluid flows is important for autonomous vehicles and active particles, but classical methods may be computationally expensive.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning to approximate the optimal policy.
result: They demonstrate that reinforcement learning can efficiently find near-optimal trajectories in various flow fields.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a practical approach to navigation in complex flows, though the work is primarily applied and does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased random walks with stochastic resetting and the resulting localization-delocalization transition, which is a topic in statistical physics.
motivation: Understanding how directional drift affects the emergence of localized stationary states in resetting random walks.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of biased random walks with resetting to previously visited sites.
result: Bias acts as a competing mechanism that can weaken or suppress localization.
conclusion: The competition between bias and resetting leads to a localization-delocalization transition in low-dimensional systems.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: To understand anomalous diffusion in complex media, particularly when transport is biased due to asymmetric distributions.
method: The authors analyze CTRW models with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions, deriving expressions for mean-squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
result: They find that asymmetry in waiting-time and jump-length distributions leads to rich transport behavior, including subdiffusion, superdiffusion, and ballistic regimes depending on the parameters.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous environments, with potential applications in physics and biology.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a stochastic system is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem.
method: The authors analyze the order statistics of Brownian particles under an asymptotically power-law confining potential, deriving universal behavior independent of the potential exponent.
result: The order statistics describing particle reshuffling are universal, while the reshuffling timescale depends on the potential exponent.
conclusion: The universality of order statistics in this system is established, providing insight into stochastic ordering dynamics.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, using numerical simulations.
motivation: To understand how hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields affect neuronal network dynamics, particularly chimera states.
method: Numerical simulations of a ring of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons with hybrid coupling and applied electric fields.
result: Observation of various collective behaviors including incoherent activity, traveling waves, and chimera/multichimera states.
conclusion: Electric fields and hybrid coupling can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in neuronal networks.

title: Realizable Entropic Lattice Boltzmann Method For high-Péclet Scalar Transport
authors: Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, And Xu Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, and Xu Chu

We present a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method (RELBM) for scalar transport at high Péclet (Pe) number. The method combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a strictly conservative population-space realizability limiter activ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013301] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for scalar transport in fluid dynamics, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To simulate high-Péclet scalar transport efficiently using a lattice Boltzmann method.
method: Combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with nonorthogonality correction and a realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stability and accuracy for high Péclet numbers.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for scalar transport simulations.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate of Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research, but existing distance measures for Markov chains have limitations.
method: The authors define a distance function using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove it satisfies metric properties.
result: The proposed distance function is a valid metric and can be computed efficiently for finite-state Markov chains.
conclusion: The distance function provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains, with potential applications in clustering and classification.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically using continued fractions and matrix methods to compute the intermediate scattering function.
result: They obtain exact expressions for the intermediate scattering function and analyze its dependence on tilt and potential strength.
conclusion: The work provides a complete analytical solution for the dynamics of a Brownian particle in a tilted periodic potential, which can be used to interpret scattering experiments.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract:
Author(s): Avadhut V. Purohit and Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top, extending the quantum kicked top with an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in periodically driven systems, which are important for quantum chaos and control.
method: The dynamics are expressed in terms of effective parameters, and analytical conditions for resonances are derived.
result: Exact quantum resonances are identified and characterized analytically.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits rich resonance behavior that can be understood through effective parameter analysis.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand how higher-order interactions can arise from simple pairwise couplings with time delay in oscillator networks.
method: The delayed pairwise coupling is expanded to second order, yielding a delay-free Kuramoto model with both pairwise and three-body interactions.
result: Numerical simulations and analysis demonstrate the emergence of three-body interactions from time-delayed pairwise coupling.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions can naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, providing a mechanism for complex dynamics in oscillator networks.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in coupled Brusselator systems, a nonlinear chemical oscillator model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamical origin of extreme events in nonlinear systems is important for predicting rare but catastrophic events in various fields.
method: The authors analyze a diffusively coupled Brusselator model, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, using statistical and dynamical systems tools.
result: They characterize extreme events by heavy-tailed probability distributions and identify dynamical mechanisms leading to their emergence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into extreme events in coupled oscillators but does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Random Walks On Disordered Lattices: The Role Of Effective Porosity, Blocked Domain Width, And Spatial Correlations
authors: Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues And Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
abstract:
Author(s): Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues and Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis

We perform a numerical study of random walks (RWs) on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, analyze the dependence of effective diffusion coefficients [MATH] on the effective porosity [MATH], and show applications to diffusive solute transport in some porous materials.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014122] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies random walks on disordered lattices to model diffusive transport in porous media, focusing on effective porosity and spatial correlations.
motivation: Understanding how disorder and spatial correlations affect diffusion in porous materials is important for applications like solute transport, but the work is purely classical and does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, analyzing effective diffusion coefficients as a function of porosity.
result: The effective diffusion coefficient depends on effective porosity and blocked domain width, with spatial correlations influencing transport.
conclusion: The study provides insights into classical diffusion in disordered media but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, And David B. Saakian
abstract:
Author(s): Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, and David B. Saakian

We are looking for different phases in hidden Markov models (HMMs). By analyzing the stationary solution of the master equation, we discover different situations with localized or delocalized distributions for the stationary distributions of the master equation. We hypothesize that these phases are …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014123] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phases and phase transitions in hidden Markov models using master equation analysis.
motivation: To identify different phases (localized vs delocalized) in hidden Markov models and understand their stationary distributions.
method: Analyzes the stationary solution of the master equation for hidden Markov models.
result: Discovers different phases with localized or delocalized stationary distributions and hypothesizes phase transition points.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of phases in HMMs but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Alternating Pattern Formation In Oscillatory Media With Spatially Uniform And Nonuniform Global Feedback
authors: Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, And Fengze Sui
abstract:
Author(s): Zhilin Qu, Chunli Huang, and Fengze Sui

Alternating (temporally period-2) stripes, clusters, and labyrinths have been observed in chemical and biochemical reactions, in Min-protein dynamics in E. coli and in vitro systems, and in calcium alternans in cardiac myocytes. However, the mechanisms underlying the formation of these spatiotempora…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014211] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies alternating pattern formation in oscillatory media with global feedback, applied to chemical and biological systems.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback.
result: Identified conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating pattern formation.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spatiotemporal pattern formation in oscillatory media.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine phase synchronization and spatial swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators are a prototypical model for active matter, but a general theoretical framework for their collective dynamics was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving low-dimensional equations for the order parameters.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for stability and bifurcations of various collective states, validated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for understanding swarmalator dynamics, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information theory and thermodynamics.

title: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz And The Prony-Ritz Equivalence Class
authors: Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, And Michael L. Wagman
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, and Michael L. Wagman

Recent work [ 112, 054506 (2025);
tldr: This paper presents a method for extracting energy spectra from correlation functions in quantum field theory using filtered Rayleigh-Ritz and Prony-Ritz techniques.
motivation: Extracting energy spectra from lattice QCD correlation functions is challenging due to noise and excited-state contamination; existing methods like the Lanczos algorithm have limitations.
method: The authors introduce a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method and a Prony-Ritz equivalence class approach to analyze correlation functions, building on recent work with the block Lanczos algorithm.
result: The proposed methods provide improved extraction of energy eigenvalues and matrix elements from correlation functions, with demonstrated accuracy in test cases.
conclusion: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz and Prony-Ritz offer robust alternatives for spectral extraction in quantum field theory, particularly for lattice QCD.

title: Intrinsic Density Of States And The Origin Of Gamma Volume Distributions In Jammed Granular Matter
authors: Ching Chang, Yang Chang, And Jason Chao
abstract:
Author(s): Ching Chang, Yang Chang, and Jason Chao

Athermal systems such as granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations despite the absence of thermal equilibration, yet a quantitative statistical-mechanical description remains incomplete. Within the Edwards ensemble, volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity and compactivity …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015410] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies volume fluctuations in jammed granular matter using the Edwards ensemble, a statistical mechanics approach for athermal systems.
motivation: Athermal granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations, but a quantitative statistical-mechanical description is lacking.
method: The authors apply the Edwards ensemble, where volume replaces energy as the conserved quantity, to derive an intrinsic density of states.
result: They obtain volume distribution functions that match experimental observations.
conclusion: The Edwards ensemble provides a valid framework for describing volume fluctuations in jammed granular matter.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Indistinguishable Energy States And The Glass Transition
authors: Shimul Akhanjee
abstract:
Author(s): Shimul Akhanjee

The statistical mechanics of particles that populate indistinguishable energy substates is explored. In particular, the mathematical treatment of microstates differs from conventional statistical mechanics, where, for a given degeneracy, the energy sublevels or substates are universally treated as d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014119] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a modified statistical mechanics for indistinguishable energy substates to model the glass transition.
motivation: Standard statistical mechanics treats degenerate energy levels as distinct, which may not capture the physics of glasses where substates are indistinguishable.
method: The author develops a formalism where microstates are counted differently when energy substates are indistinguishable, leading to a modified partition function.
result: The new approach yields a thermodynamic description that exhibits a glass transition-like behavior.
conclusion: Indistinguishability of energy substates may be a key ingredient for understanding the glass transition from first principles.

title: Twisted State Stability Under Local Order Parameter Adaptation
authors: Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, And Ya Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Xueqin Wang, Hong He, Wende Tang, Yiju Peng, and Ya Jia

Twisted states commonly arise in nonlocally coupled ring networks. We study the stability of twisted states in networks with higher-order interactions under the adaptive mechanism based on the local order parameter. The adaptive feedback dynamically regulates the coupling strength and thus reshapes …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of twisted states in nonlocally coupled ring networks with higher-order interactions and adaptive coupling based on local order parameters.
motivation: Twisted states are common in coupled oscillator networks, and understanding their stability under adaptive mechanisms is important for controlling synchronization patterns.
method: The authors analyze the stability of twisted states using linear stability analysis and numerical simulations, incorporating higher-order interactions and adaptive feedback that adjusts coupling strength based on local order parameters.
result: They find that the adaptive mechanism can stabilize or destabilize twisted states depending on parameters, and higher-order interactions modify the stability boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of complex networks with adaptive coupling, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Energy-dynamics Interplay In Temporal Networks Triggers Explosive Synchronization
authors: Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, And Thierry Njougouo
abstract:
Author(s): Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, and Thierry Njougouo

Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in the study of collective behavior. In this paper we investigate the synchronization transition in networks of coupled dynamical systems from an energetic perspective. Interactions between systems/oscillators are assumed to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive synchronization in temporal networks from an energetic perspective, focusing on the interplay between energy dynamics and network topology.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions in complex networks is fundamental to collective behavior, and the role of energy dynamics in such transitions is not well understood.
method: The authors model coupled dynamical systems with time-varying interactions and analyze the synchronization transition using energetic measures and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the interplay between energy dynamics and temporal network structure can trigger explosive synchronization, a first-order transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how energy considerations affect synchronization in temporal networks, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Nanorotator In The Hypomagnetic Field: Implications For Magnetobiology
authors: V. N. Binhi
abstract:
Author(s): V. N. Binhi

A mechanism for the biological effects of the hypomagnetic field is proposed, based on the rotational motion of a molecule as a whole within a cavity in an enzyme. It has been shown previously that a molecular rotator about 1 nm in size can have a decoherence time of up to tens of milliseconds. On s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014406] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum nanorotator mechanism for biological effects of hypomagnetic fields.
motivation: To explain how weak magnetic fields can affect biological systems via quantum rotational dynamics.
method: Models a molecular rotator in an enzyme cavity with decoherence times up to tens of milliseconds.
result: The rotator's quantum behavior may be influenced by hypomagnetic fields, leading to biological effects.
conclusion: Quantum nanorotators could mediate magnetobiological effects, but the mechanism remains speculative.

title: Hamiltonian Active Particles In Incompressible Fluid Membranes
authors: Sneha Krishnan And Rickmoy Samanta
abstract:
Author(s): Sneha Krishnan and Rickmoy Samanta

Active proteins and membrane-bound motors exert force dipole flows along fluid interfaces and lipid bilayers. We develop a Hamiltonian framework for the interactions of pusher and puller dipoles embedded in an incompressible two-dimensional membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase. Beginning…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015102] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a Hamiltonian framework for active particles in fluid membranes, focusing on hydrodynamic interactions in a biological context.
motivation: To understand the interactions of active proteins and membrane-bound motors in incompressible fluid membranes, which is relevant to biological systems.
method: The authors develop a Hamiltonian formalism for pusher and puller dipoles embedded in a 2D membrane supported by a shallow viscous subphase.
result: The framework captures the dynamics of active particles in membranes, including force dipole flows.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for studying active matter in biological membranes, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Polarization Conversion In Time-modulated Magnetized Plasmas: Faraday Configuration
authors: Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, And Mark A. Cappelli
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Mehrpour Bernety, Dikshitulu K. Kalluri, and Mark A. Cappelli

In this paper, we address the problem of wave propagation within an unbounded time-modulated magnetized plasma in a Faraday configuration. We present an analysis formulated by coupling Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic evolution equation for the plasma current density, and casting the result…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave propagation in time-modulated magnetized plasmas, focusing on polarization conversion in the Faraday configuration.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in time-varying plasmas is important for applications in plasma diagnostics and communication, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors couple Maxwell's equations with the hydrodynamic plasma current equation and solve for wave propagation in a time-modulated magnetized plasma.
result: The analysis yields conditions for polarization conversion and wave behavior under time modulation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into classical wave propagation in plasmas but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for combinatorial reasoning in large language models, using a quantum computer to solve optimization problems derived from reasoning aggregation.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks that require combinatorial optimization; the authors aim to leverage quantum computing to enhance reasoning capabilities.
method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem, which is then solved on a real quantum computer using variational algorithms.
result: The approach demonstrates improved performance on certain reasoning benchmarks compared to classical baselines, though scalability remains limited by current quantum hardware.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial reasoning can augment LLMs for specific tasks, but practical deployment requires further advances in quantum hardware and algorithm efficiency.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays
authors: Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, And J. V. Alvarez
abstract:
Author(s): Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, and J. V. Alvarez

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations reveal the hydrodynamic coupling and identify the lift mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using lattice-Boltzmann simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and particle currents.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and active matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model the hydrodynamic coupling between rotating colloids and obstacles.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents arising from the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in obstacle arrays, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Jozani and Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing the probability distribution of detection times in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are several inequivalent proposals for computing detection time distributions, and the authors aim to compare them for a specific scenario.
method: The authors compute the detection time distribution for a quantum particle using three different approaches: two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
result: The paper presents the computed distributions and likely discusses differences among the proposals.
conclusion: The comparison helps clarify the predictions of different detection time models, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Luning Zhao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Luning Zhao et al.

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for quantum chemistry using matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers.
motivation: To model chemical reaction barriers efficiently using near-term quantum devices.
method: Combines auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo with quantum tomography via matchgate shadows on a trapped ion quantum computer.
result: Demonstrates an end-to-end workflow for computing reaction barriers.
conclusion: The approach shows promise for practical quantum chemistry on current hardware.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:
Author(s): L. A. Rüffert and T. E. Mehlstäubler

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical or mesoscopic physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved interfaces using self-organized ion crystals as a model system.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap, observing concentric shell structures and measuring friction between shells.
result: Observation of shell formation and measurement of two-dimensional nanofriction properties in the ion crystal system.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for studying nanofriction, but the work does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect that allows selective polarization of Kramers partnered states.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs, which may have applications in spintronics or optoelectronics, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that heavy-tailed fluctuations can arise from non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: To explain the origin of heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics observed in various fields without invoking criticality.
method: The authors analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and demonstrate a mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification that generates heavy tails.
result: Heavy-tailed behavior emerges from non-normal amplification even when the system is far from instability, providing a universal mechanism.
conclusion: Non-normal eigenvector amplification is a robust mechanism for heavy-tailed fluctuations, applicable across physics, finance, and economics.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions, a condensed matter system not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the effects of frustration and anisotropic interactions in a controlled colloidal system, which can be visualized in real time.
method: The authors modify artificial colloidal ice by inducing anisotropic interactions and observe the resulting dynamics.
result: Anisotropic interactions induce dynamical spin freezing in the artificial colloidal ice system.
conclusion: The study provides insights into frustration and dynamics in colloidal systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, and Salvador Miret-Artés

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas. We consider that chiral molecules are formed resonantly via ultracold collisions of achiral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033056] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical mechanism to detect parity violation in chiral molecules via ultracold gas amplification.
motivation: Parity-violating energy differences in chiral molecules are extremely small and hard to measure directly; the authors aim to amplify the effect to observable levels.
method: They model ultracold collisions of achiral fragments that form chiral molecules, and show that a tiny PVED can lead to a macroscopic enantiomeric excess due to quantum statistical effects.
result: The mechanism predicts that an initial achiral mixture can evolve into a significant enantiomeric excess, indirectly revealing the PVED.
conclusion: This provides a new route to measure parity violation in molecular systems, but the work is primarily in molecular physics and quantum chemistry, not directly aligned with the user's quantum information or thermodynamics interests.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, and Tomáš Bzdušek

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain 2D Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the emergence of flat bands and topological states in tree-like structures that mimic 2D lattices, which may have implications for novel phases of matter.
method: The authors derive exact analytical solutions for the tight-binding models on decorated Cayley trees using recursive techniques and symmetry arguments.
result: They obtain the complete energy spectrum and identify flat bands and topological edge states in these tree analogs.
conclusion: Decorated Cayley trees provide a solvable platform to study flat bands and topology, but the work is primarily a mathematical physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid
abstract:
Author(s): Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, and Nicole Abaid

Collective motion in active matter can arise from interaction rules that generate group-level order. A seminal example is the Vicsek model, which describes flocking using a simple local alignment rule. Despite three decades of research, the network topology induced by the particles’ alignment remain…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules lead to group-level order in active matter systems is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze the network topology induced by particle alignment in the Vicsek model, examining cluster properties across different scales.
result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing scale-dependent behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the structure of collective motion but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving
authors: Fumiya Sekiguchi, Yuta Murotani, And Ryo Shimano
abstract:
