Nonequilibrium states of matter, when driven periodically, can exhibit exotic properties and emergent behaviors that are fundamentally distinct from those in equilibrium systems. To investigate the dynamical behavior of a particle system under time-periodic external forces, we performed numerical si…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033041] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system under periodic driving, using numerical simulations.
motivation: To explore emergent nonequilibrium behaviors in periodically driven systems that are distinct from equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic properties like bistability and even-order harmonics in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Quantum Physics-informed Neural Network With Residual-based Adaptive Refinement For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, And Zhichao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, and Zhichao Zhang

In this paper, we propose a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by using residual-based adaptive refinement (RAR). The method incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of QPINN, which aims to enhance conver…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033042] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum physics-informed neural network with residual-based adaptive refinement for solving partial differential equations.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving PDEs but suffer from slow convergence and accuracy issues; quantum neural networks may offer advantages.
method: The authors design a quantum neural network architecture and incorporate a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism (RAR) to focus training on regions with high residual error.
result: The QPINN with RAR achieves improved convergence and accuracy compared to standard PINNs on benchmark PDEs.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks combined with adaptive sampling can effectively solve PDEs, though practical quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They introduce Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog Floquet solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator-based Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet-based Ising machines with amplitude modulations offer a practical way to enhance optimization performance.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are exotic phases of matter that host anyonic excitations, but experimental realization has been challenging.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy was used to measure the out-of-plane magneto-optical response of the MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: An out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response was observed, providing evidence for a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest that twisted MoTe2 is a promising platform for realizing fractional topological insulators.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields backreacting on classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum mechanics with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum field theory and general relativity by allowing matter to remain quantum while spacetime is treated classically, providing a testable framework for quantum gravity.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime background, incorporating backreaction effects through a consistent semiclassical approach.
result: They derive a mathematical framework that yields well-defined dynamics for the combined system, including a consistent treatment of the backreaction of quantum fields on the classical metric.
conclusion: The framework offers a potential avenue for testing whether spacetime is fundamentally classical or quantum, and provides a basis for further theoretical and experimental investigations.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics using large language models.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific process, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing specific research directions in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; this gap needed to be bridged.
method: The authors develop new computational complexity arguments, likely involving approximate counting and average-case hardness, to prove that BosonSampling with linear modes remains hard.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is computationally hard, providing theoretical justification for near-term photonic quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work validates that photonic quantum advantage experiments in the saturated regime are indeed classically hard, strengthening the case for BosonSampling as a demonstration of quantum supremacy.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and identifies ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism is a key dynamical feature underlying abrupt learning in recurrent networks.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantization of chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons, which are topological excitations in spin chains, and their experimental signatures.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their low-energy excitations.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: These solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a way to observe quantum soliton dynamics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories and uncovers emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories in three dimensions, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel numerical approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs on a sphere.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying 3D fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a general feature of such theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré materials is important for potential information manipulation, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for designing materials with spin moiré superstructures, but does not directly contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The stability of topological magnon gaps at high temperatures provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision finding in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that uses physical principles to infer causal relationships from time-series data of networked systems.
result: The framework successfully identifies causal links across various networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a physics-based tool for network inference, applicable to diverse fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.

conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

result: The system undergoes a three-dimensional XY universality class transition, and the ground state shows hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.

authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe

motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under varying electric fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control enables transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
motivation: To understand how hyperuniformity, a property of suppressed density fluctuations, affects critical behavior at the liquid-vapor phase transition.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the thermodynamics and fluctuations of hyperuniform fluids near the critical point.
result: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform systems, with implications for materials design.

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the resulting complex domain structures.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study the material Ni2MnSe2O3, identifying a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality.
result: The study identifies a uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality, leading to the formation of complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of ferro-rotational order and its interplay with other ferroic orders, which may have implications for multiferroic materials and domain engineering.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing, but lacks specific technical contributions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with broad fundamental and applied interest.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field-theoretic techniques.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review that applies quantum field theory methods (e.g., path integrals, Doi-Peliti formalism) to classical stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion systems, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond chemistry to ecology and epidemiology.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is important for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave signals (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to theoretical nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized, and compared to predictions from nuclear theory.
conclusion: Current observations provide important constraints on the dense matter equation of state, with future observations expected to further refine our understanding.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and simulation studies of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The review tracks progress from the inception of the field to the present day and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued synergy between approaches is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological characteristics of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with ongoing experimental and theoretical developments, offering insights into frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on future directions for integrating these models into practical applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are advancing, but further development is needed to fully exploit them in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications in spintronics.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for next-generation memory and logic devices due to their topological stability and small size. Understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing spintronics.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum tunneling, and interactions with electrons and magnons, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights that skyrmions exhibit quantum phenomena such as tunneling and superposition, and that their topological charge influences transport properties.
conclusion: Quantum effects in skyrmions open new avenues for quantum spintronics, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review covers a wide range of experimental constraints on spin-dependent interactions and discusses the potential of future experiments to discover new physics.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for exploring physics beyond the standard model, and ongoing experimental efforts may reveal new particles or forces.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to new materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity, homogeneity) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made under conditions that violate the assumptions of the bounds, and shows how designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplication of bounds; this insight can guide development of materials with enhanced properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for simulating quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various physical platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries offers a promising avenue for studying fundamental physics, but the field is still developing.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review explores the interface between quantum mechanics and gravity using massive quantum systems as probes.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature or modifications.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation by gravity.
result: Current experiments are testing whether gravity causes decoherence or mediates entanglement, but no definitive conclusion yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity effects, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Atomic Clock Frequency Ratios With Fractional Uncertainty $≤3.2×{10}^{−18}$
authors: Alexander Aeppli et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Aeppli et al. (BACON Collaboration)

We report high-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks based on [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. With total fractional uncertainties at or below [MATH], these measurements meet an important milestone criterion for redefinit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033201] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: High-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks with fractional uncertainty at or below 3.2×10^{-18}.
motivation: To meet a milestone criterion for redefinition of the SI second based on optical clocks.
method: Frequency ratio measurements using optical atomic clocks based on different atomic species.
result: Achieved total fractional uncertainties at or below 3.2×10^{-18}.
conclusion: These measurements support the potential redefinition of the SI second.

title: Interelectronic Correlation: Neutral And Ionized Atoms In Conjugate Spaces
authors: M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, And J. C. Angulo
abstract:
Author(s): M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, and J. C. Angulo

The intercorrelation level among constituent electrons of a multielectronic system is quantified by comparing the electron-pair density and the product of its marginal one-particle densities. The resulting comparison is interpreted as a measure of the interelectronic correlation and/or mutual inform…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012812] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies interelectronic correlation in atoms by comparing electron-pair densities with product of one-particle densities, using conjugate spaces.
motivation: To develop a measure of interelectronic correlation and mutual information in multielectronic systems.
method: Comparison of electron-pair density and product of marginal one-particle densities in both position and momentum spaces.
result: A quantitative measure of interelectronic correlation is obtained.
conclusion: The approach provides insight into electron correlation in neutral and ionized atoms.

title: Parametric Mössbauer Radiation In The Grazing-diffraction Geometry: Specular Diffraction And Superradiant Amplification
authors: Ze-An Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, And Jörg Evers
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-an Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, and Jörg Evers

Parametric x-ray radiation (PXR) is a tunable and versatile x-ray production mechanism that relies on relativistic electrons traversing through a crystal. When the crystal contains Mössbauer nuclei, they may also contribute to the x-ray generation, giving rise to spectrally narrow parametric Mössbau…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013115] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parametric Mössbauer radiation in grazing-diffraction geometry, focusing on specular diffraction and superradiant amplification.
motivation: To explore a new x-ray production mechanism that combines parametric x-ray radiation with Mössbauer nuclei for spectrally narrow emission.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the grazing-diffraction geometry for parametric Mössbauer radiation, deriving expressions for the radiation field and considering superradiant amplification.
result: They find that specular diffraction can enhance the radiation and that superradiant amplification occurs under certain conditions.
conclusion: The proposed geometry offers a way to generate narrow-band x-rays with potential applications in nuclear resonance and quantum optics.

title: Kinetic Instability And Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{Li}}_{2}{\mathrm{AuH}}_{6}$ And ${\mathrm{Li}}_{2}{\mathrm{AgH}}_{6}$ At Ambient Pressure
authors: Yucheng Ding, Haoran Chen, And Junren Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Ding, Haoran Chen, and Junren Shi

[MATH] and [MATH] have been proposed as promising candidates for high-temperature superconductors under ambient pressure. While previous studies confirm the dynamic stability of these two thermodynamically unstable systems, their kinetic …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014508] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the kinetic stability and superconductivity of Li2AuH6 and Li2AgH6 at ambient pressure using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To identify high-temperature superconductors that are stable under ambient pressure, which is crucial for practical applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to evaluate kinetic stability and superconducting properties.
result: Both Li2AuH6 and Li2AgH6 are predicted to be high-temperature superconductors with kinetic stability at ambient pressure.
conclusion: These materials are promising candidates for ambient-pressure high-temperature superconductivity, warranting further experimental investigation.

title: Atomic-scale Origin Of Polarity At ${01\overline{1}8}$ Twin Walls In Calcite
authors: Tomohiro Yamashita, Soma Seto, Yixin Lin, Yang Yang, Xiangdong Ding, Nicholas J. Butterfield, Ekhard Salje, Taro Kuwano, And Hiroko Yokota
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Yamashita, Soma Seto, Yixin Lin, Yang Yang, Xiangdong Ding, Nicholas J. Butterfield, Ekhard Salje, Taro Kuwano, and Hiroko Yokota

We report a combined experimental and computational study of the polar nature of twin walls (TWs) in calcite. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) imaging reveals that [MATH] TWs exhibit clear second-harmonic activity, whereas [MATH] TWs show no detectable response under any p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024106] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the atomic-scale origin of polarity at twin walls in calcite using SHG imaging and DFT calculations.
motivation: Understanding the polar nature of twin walls in minerals like calcite is important for materials science and geophysics.
method: The authors combine second-harmonic generation (SHG) imaging with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to analyze twin walls in calcite.
result: They find that certain twin walls exhibit second-harmonic activity, indicating polarity, while others do not, and explain the origin at the atomic scale.
conclusion: The polarity of twin walls in calcite arises from specific atomic arrangements, which can be predicted and controlled.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on higher-order networks with nonlinear adaptation, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation affect explosive transitions in spreading processes on networks.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for spreading dynamics on simplicial complexes with nonlinear adaptation rules and analyze the conditions for explosive transitions.
result: Nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation play a crucial role in shaping spreading dynamics, offering insights for controlling epidemic or information spread.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, And M. Wollenhaupt
abstract:
Author(s): D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, and M. Wollenhaupt

We employ, for the first time, bichromatic three-dimensional (3D) polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields in atomic multiphoton ionization to create previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets. The 3D fields are created by the noncollinear superposition of two polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033048] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the use of bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To explore new regimes of light-matter interaction by shaping the polarization of ultrashort laser pulses in three dimensions, enabling control over electron wave packets.
method: Noncollinear superposition of two polarization-shaped laser pulses to generate 3D fields, applied to multiphoton ionization of atoms.
result: Observation of previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets, demonstrating control over electron dynamics.
conclusion: Three-dimensional polarization shaping offers a new tool for manipulating electron wave packets in strong-field physics.

title: Moiré-resonant Surface State In Ultrathin ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}(110)$
authors: Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, And Simon Moser
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, and Simon Moser

[MATH] has emerged as a prototypical candidate for altermagnetism. In the face of daunting evidence for magnetic order in the bulk, the focus naturally shifted to surfaces and ultrathin films, where Coulomb interactions are dimensionally quenched and electron correlations strongly enha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033058] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of ultrathin RuO2(110) films, focusing on moiré-resonant surface states and altermagnetism.
motivation: RuO2 is a candidate altermagnet, but surface and thin-film properties are poorly understood due to enhanced correlations.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: Observation of moiré-resonant surface states and evidence of altermagnetic order in ultrathin films.
conclusion: Ultrathin RuO2(110) exhibits altermagnetic surface states with potential for spintronic applications.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in van der Waals heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time-resolved spectroscopy and theoretical modeling to study charge transfer dynamics at different excitation energies.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways that depend on excitation energy, revealing how energy influences charge transfer efficiency.
conclusion: Controlling excitation energy can tune charge transfer pathways, offering a route to optimize device performance.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands exist only at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature stable platform.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT).
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are robust at room temperature, with orbital selectivity and tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics at room temperature, potentially enabling practical applications.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale silicon photonic crystals are fabricated and characterized experimentally, with theoretical modeling of radiative loss effects.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is observed and attributed to radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of radiative loss in disordered photonic crystals and have implications for photonic device design.

title: Truncated Photon
authors: Isak Cecil Onsager Rukan, Jan Gulla, And Johannes Skaar
abstract:
Author(s): Isak Cecil Onsager Rukan, Jan Gulla, and Johannes Skaar

Removing a mirror while a single photon is in the process of reflecting creates a quantum state of countless photons, theorists say.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies the quantum state resulting from suddenly removing a mirror during single-photon reflection, predicting a multi-photon state.
motivation: To explore the effect of a time-dependent boundary condition on a single-photon field, which is a fundamental quantum optics problem.
method: The authors model the mirror removal as a sudden change in boundary conditions and solve the quantum field evolution.
result: The process generates a state containing multiple photons, with a specific photon number distribution.
conclusion: The phenomenon illustrates non-trivial quantum optics effects from dynamical boundaries, but has no direct connection to the specified research directions.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction in layered materials is important for nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer interactions.
result: They find that electric fields can modulate interlayer binding and sliding energy barriers, enabling control of friction.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route to tune friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Periodic Gravitational Lensing With Oscillating Boson Stars
authors: Xing-Yu Yang (杨星宇), Tan Chen (陈坦), And Rong-Gen Cai
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Yu Yang (杨星宇), Tan Chen (陈坦), and Rong-Gen Cai (蔡荣根)

We show that oscillating (real-scalar) boson stars generically host an oscillating radial caustic. Sources near this caustic cross it every half period, thereby producing periodic caustic-crossing lensing. The resulting observables are phase locked to the lens oscillation: image-pair creation or ann…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031403] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies periodic gravitational lensing caused by oscillating boson stars, a topic in astrophysics.
motivation: To investigate observable effects of oscillating boson stars, which are hypothetical compact objects.
method: The authors analyze the lensing properties of oscillating real-scalar boson stars, identifying an oscillating radial caustic and computing image pair creation/annihilation.
result: They find that sources near the caustic produce periodic lensing events phase-locked to the boson star oscillation.
conclusion: Oscillating boson stars can generate unique periodic gravitational lensing signatures that may be detectable.

title: Emergent Trion Resonance Driven By Lattice Reconstruction In A Moiré Superlattice
authors: Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. Macdonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, And Xiaoqin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. MacDonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, and Xiaoqin Li

We investigate how many-electron excited states emerge in twisted [MATH] homobilayers when the lattice reconstructions evolve. Notably, we identify a new trion resonance that arises in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, where gradual changes in atomic alignment between t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036902] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent trion resonances in twisted MoSe2 homobilayers driven by lattice reconstruction, focusing on many-body excited states in moiré superlattices.
motivation: Understanding how lattice reconstruction affects many-electron excited states in moiré materials is crucial for tailoring their optical and electronic properties.
method: The authors combine optical spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and first-principles calculations to investigate the evolution of trion resonances as a function of twist angle and lattice relaxation.
result: A new trion resonance is identified in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, correlated with gradual changes in atomic alignment between layers.
conclusion: Lattice reconstruction plays a key role in determining the many-body excited states in moiré superlattices, and the discovered trion resonance provides insight into the interplay between structural and electronic degrees of freedom.

title: Probing Dielectric Screening In Van Der Waals Heterostructures Via Pressure-Tuned Exciton Rydberg Series
authors: Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, And Clément Faugeras
abstract:
Author(s): Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, and Clément Faugeras

Excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors are directly exposed to the environment and are sensitive to the dielectric properties of their surrounding. Here, we show that the Rydberg series of excited states of excitons in a monolayer [MATH] encapsulated in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036903] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures by measuring pressure-tuned exciton Rydberg series in monolayer MoSe2 encapsulated in hBN.
motivation: Excitons in 2D semiconductors are sensitive to the dielectric environment, and understanding screening is crucial for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors apply hydrostatic pressure to tune the dielectric properties of the hBN environment and measure the exciton Rydberg series using optical spectroscopy.
result: They observe a pressure-dependent shift of exciton excited states, which allows them to extract the dielectric screening and its effect on the Rydberg series.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a method to probe and control dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures via pressure, relevant for 2D material physics.

title: Extending Ground-Based Gravitational-Wave Sensitivity To 5 Hz
authors: Amit Singh Ubhi, Lari Koponen, Jiri Smetana, Yulin Xia, Haixing Miao, Emilia Chick, John Bryant, Geraint Pratten, Teng Zhang, Richard Mittleman, Peter Fritschel, Alan V. Cumming, Giles Hammond, And Denis Martynov
abstract:

motivation: Conflicting reports exist on the ground state of CeRhSn2, which has a sawtooth arrangement of Ce sites suggesting geometric magnetic frustration.

result: They found that CeRhSn2 exhibits two magnetic transitions and a complex magnetic phase diagram, with evidence of frustration and possible quadrupolar order.
conclusion: The study resolves previous discrepancies and establishes CeRhSn2 as a frustrated magnet with potential for further study of exotic magnetic phases.

result: Na doping increases the carrier concentration and enhances metallicity, but no superconductivity is observed at ambient pressure.
conclusion: While Na doping improves metallicity, it does not induce superconductivity at ambient pressure, suggesting that other factors are needed to achieve superconductivity in this system.

result: They identify and quantify the cubic magneto-optic Kerr effect contributions, showing their dependence on crystallographic orientation.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive experimental characterization of higher-order magneto-optic effects in nickel, which can inform applications in magneto-optics and spintronics.

result: They observed twofold degenerate acoustic Landau levels and pseudospin-dependent transport, confirming the theoretical predictions.

motivation: Understanding the optical properties of calcium fluoride is important for applications in optics and atom-surface interactions, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a compact functional form for the dielectric function based on temperature-dependent IR and UV peaks, and compute atom-surface interactions using the Lifshitz theory.
result: The model accurately reproduces experimental data for the dielectric function and predicts temperature-dependent Casimir-Polder potentials.
conclusion: The work provides a useful tool for calculating atom-surface interactions, but it is purely a materials science and condensed matter physics study.

motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering measurements on liquid hydrogen sulfide to probe its collective dynamics in the THz range.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of hydrogen-bonded liquids.
